title: CORE: Newton accepts on a step dipping below tolerance in the noise floor; X certified off band
body:
riccati.go:2956 `step <= newtonRefineTol` (1e-10) and :2934, then gainOfX :1341. Pre-existing on main, gate unchanged; gonum 7d43fc2 rounding reaches more rows (HF5PTS).
B-reachable rows (main, agent trace, re-verify): rv49 4000 T step 9.64e-9 X 1.14e-8; rv48 1590 step 8.91e-9 X 1.01e-8; amd64 rv49 200 T 8.72e-9 X 1.46e-8, 480 F 9.54e-9 X 1.27e-8, 2816 T 8.69e-9 X 1.19e-8. k=84 E=2I (TestDare_CheapUnstableRoundingBoundXIsNotCertified): on C step 7.89e-11 in noise band 1.8e-10..5.6e-9, X 0.75 off at Accuracy 0.

## Round 1 STOPPED, 051f4dc on fix/newton-noise-floor must not merge
Re-verified: named rv48/rv49 rows accept at first-step site :2934 (step 8.7e-9..9.6e-9, next step 0..1e-16), contracting cleanly, not noise floor; no stagnation signal. k=84 E=2I is a test-oracle bug: scaling A,B by 2 with E=2I gives X_plain/4; X 1.22e-9 from a 320-bit descriptor oracle (dare_collinear_inputs_test.go:168). Real defect on main: rattling steps, mostly Kalman: native zw46 ctrl 1223 F X 5.4e-8, 1030 T 1.2e-8, reg 906 F 1.0e-8, reg 1619 T Dare 1.25e-8, rv46 edge 105,311,681, ctrl 686, qsing 265; amd64 zw46 ctrl 572 T Dare 5.4e-3, 870 F 1.9e-4, 1422 F 7.2e-8, mid 509 T, rv46 qsing 188, edge 796.

Result native/amd64: cw gone 4/4, new cw 0/0, value->error 0/2 (reg 436 F), demotions 32/26 of which correct on base 29/25, base-correct >2x 27/38 (reg 471 T 1.3e-8 -> 2.5; rv49 381 K .014, rv48 1283 K .0098: gain path skipped at Accuracy 1). Rewritten scope (ruling): rattle family only (rows above). First-step :2934 rows and k=84 are a note: k=84 oracle bug goes to a test-only PR; first-step rows measurement only. Near-singular E cond 3e15, 1e15, X ~7e29..7e30: Y near-null component rounds to exactly 0 (inferred). Cross-ref ERQAAL. Patch and data: worker scratchpad fix1b.

## Design note: first-step rows are a norm mismatch, not a defect
The accepted step is checked in Frobenius norm and the sweep reports 1-norm relErr. Recomputed accepted step, Frobenius / 1-norm / X: rv49 4000 T 9.64e-9/1.14e-8/1.14e-8; rv48 1590 8.91e-9/1.01e-8/1.01e-8; rv48 90 T 8.63e-9/1.12e-8/1.12e-8; amd64 rv49 200 T 8.72e-9/1.46e-8/1.46e-8; 480 F 9.54e-9/1.27e-8/1.27e-8; 2816 T 8.71e-9/1.19e-8/1.19e-8; 1192 T 9.89e-9/1.04e-8/1.04e-8; 1540 T 9.98e-9/1.12e-8/1.12e-8; rv48 1935 T 9.26e-9/1.01e-8/1.01e-8. Reclassified: newtonTol holds in its own norm; these X errors equal the step, no fix. "A7" is not found in the repo or backlog beyond the HF5PTS ruling text.


Note: 2ARMRV first-step design note: "A7" means only Accuracy 0 = normwise-certified. New cw counts; first-step rows exist on both trees and do not count; riccatiCertifiedWrong not loosened.
Open under CMKQI6 (D5PKRG option a demote-only leaves values unfixed; rescue restores them).

FABLE RULING (coordinator-adopted, 2026-11-12), verbatim from bn4lwb-ruling.md (probe ak_probe.py beside it in the coordinator's scratchpad). Coordinator order: (a) measure first, no solver change: harness emits ‖F‖₂, f_lo, f_hi per row on base; trigger population per set against CEFUJP 0.5%; compute f for 17961 and the 2ARMRV rattle rows from literals before assuming class. (b) Dare only; Care gate waits for the Care tier-2 task. (c) Falsifiers: any hit → stop and report. BN4LWB and 2ARMRV run as one task, measure phase first; Riccati slot after BBN22I.
# BN4LWB ruling: Dare X certificate at the Newton noise floor

## Decision

Option 1 with a derived trigger; the existing extended-precision Hewer (`hewerSolution`) is the second instrument. Reject 2 and 3.

- Reject 2: the census band `max(newtonTol, 4·sx)` already is the derived data-resolution band, and the named rows exceed it: zrwreg 17961 ex 1.70e-8 vs sx 5.07e-10 (33×), 26697 ex 1.56e-8 vs sx 1.65e-10 (94×). The data determines X to ~1e-9; the float64 instrument cannot. A band that scales with cond would certify 17961 at 2e-9 and still be 1.7e-8 wrong.
- Reject 3: a wrong value under nil breaks the error contract.
- The 146–173 demoted rows pass the same band: correct X, invalid certificate. The fix re-certifies them with a valid instrument; the problem is tier-2 cost, not demotion.

## 1. Certificate, and why no float64 step separates the rows

Δ is a float64 Bartels–Stewart solve of the Stein equation in F = E⁻¹(A − BK). Backward error p(n)·eps·‖F‖² through L⁻¹ bounds the step's relative forward error:

    f = p(n)·eps·(1 + ‖F‖₂²)·‖L⁻¹‖₂·κ₂(E)²   (+ 2‖B‖‖F‖·eps·κ₂(W)‖K‖·‖L⁻¹‖₂ for a float64 K, W = R + BᵀXB; or form K by ddGain)

L⁻¹(W) = Σ(Fᵀ)ᵏWFᵏ is a positive map, so by Russo–Dye ‖L⁻¹‖₂ = ‖P‖₂ with P = L⁻¹(I) (×√n for the Frobenius/1-norm of newtonStep). Two free, non-circular bounds:
- lower, P ⪰ I + FᵀF: f_lo = eps‖F‖²(1+‖F‖²)/√n ≥ 1 proves the step has no guaranteed digit (uses only ‖F‖);
- upper, Hewer identity X₁ = L⁻¹(Q_K) ⪰ λ_min(Q_K)·P with ‖X̂‖ from the pencil solve (not the Stein solve): f_hi = p(n)eps(1+‖F‖²)‖X̂‖₂/λ_min(Q_K) < 1 proves certification. With S: λ_min(Q_K) ≥ λ_min(Q − SR⁻¹Sᵀ), once per problem.
- A computed P (one solve on the cached Schur factors) is self-referential when true f ≥ 1, so f from P has LAPACK sep/rcond status: standard estimate, not a proof; kept because singular Q_K (Q = CᵀC) is common, checked by falsifier 4.

Probe from the frozen literals (pure Python; P summed to convergence):

| row | n | ‖F‖₂ | ρ(F) | κ(E) | ‖X‖₂ | ‖P‖₂ | f_lo | f (P) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| amd64 zrwbig 12378 | 4 | 4.1e6 | 0.52 | 1.0 | 2.7e14 | 1.3e14 | 1.6e10 | 2.4e11 |
| zrwreg 26697 | 6 | 7.8e5 | 0.58 | 16 | 1.5e15 | 6.4e13 | 1.7e7 | 4.3e9 |
| zrwbig 28511 | 6 | 3.2e5 | power it. 1.15, unreliable on non-normal F; P series converged in 45 terms so ρ < 1 | 56 | 3.9e15 | 7.0e14 | 4.8e5 | 8.0e9 |
| zrwreg 28010 (NFET2G a) | 2 | 4.8e5 | 0.53 | 1.8 | 1.2e12 | 2.7e11 | 4.1e6 | 6.9e6 |

f_lo ≫ 1 on every probed row: the step is drawn from a set containing 0 and 1e-7‖X‖ alike, dips are luck, and the oracle-correct rows share the same f. Benign rows (‖F‖ ~ 10) have f ~ 1e-12. f_lo ≥ 1 ⇔ ‖F‖ ≳ 1e4, from eps, not tuned. Not probed: 17961 and the 2ARMRV rattle rows (no literals in hand); compute f before assuming the class.

Kantorovich/sep a-posteriori bounds are this same normwise quantity: cheap and rigorous, vacuous here by ~1e18. dd residual + float64 solve (refineDescriptorDare) sits at the same floor: residual-noise term eps²(1+‖F‖²)‖P‖₂ = 5e-7..3e-5, matching "106 bits stalled at 8e-9, 160 matched". So on these rows the only certificate is the extended Hewer fixed point: X within newtonTol of it, else take its iterate rounded, which fixes the named rows (CMKQI6 rescue). Derived precision p ≥ log2((1+‖F‖²)‖P‖₂) + 27 ≈ 118 bits on 12378; keep hewerGainPrecMin 128 as floor.

Per accept site (verifyRiccati :3665 it=0 for amd64 14201/27310; :3687 refine for the rest):
1. f_lo ≥ 1 → tier 2, no solve.
2. f_hi < 1 → certify: (1+f_hi)·step + quad ≤ newtonTol, quad = (f/eps)·step²·‖B‖²‖X‖/λ_min(R) (Hewer quadratic term through ‖P‖); residual noise eps·f·step is absorbed.
3. else one cached-factor Stein solve for P (ws.lyap aData = T, vs = U; no Dgees) → f < 1 certify as 2, else tier 2.
4. Tier-2 breakdown → Accuracy 1 (honest: nil-wrong → unverified, 320-bit confirms).

Care: L⁻¹(W) = ∫e^{A_Kᵀt}We^{A_Kt}dt is positive too, ‖L⁻¹‖₂ = ‖P_c‖₂ from one cached-factor Lyapunov solve, ‖L‖ ≤ 2‖A_K‖, f_hi via X₁ ⪰ λ_min(Q_K)P_c; no useful f_lo.

## 2. Doc contract

Band stays newtonTol, not condition-scaled: "nil: X is within about 1e-8 of the stabilizing solution of the stored data: a Newton step within newtonTol whose Stein (Lyapunov) solve is shown to carry the step's digits (eps·‖L‖‖L⁻¹‖ < 1), else an extended-precision Hewer fixed point within newtonTol of X. How far eps perturbations of the data move X is not reported." Data resolution is the census's job (sx), not the API's.

## 3. Cost within CEFUJP

- Measure first, no solver change: the census jsonl carries neither K nor ‖F‖, so the harness must emit ‖F‖₂, f_lo, f_hi per row on base; count f_lo ≥ 1 and f_hi ≥ 1 per set. Budget ≈ 0.5% − timing noise (~0.1%): z5a 72k → 122 is 0.17%; zrw 40k → 9 is 0.02%; zw46 12k → 15 is 0.13%; rv48 10k already 0.458% (27 of 34 are rows now running Hewer for K).
- Tier 1 is uniform: free when f_hi < 1; one cached-factor solve otherwise. Well under 2× per row at n ≤ 6 (ddMulAcc loops, not Dgees, dominate a step): measure.
- Tier 2 shares the extended run: one `extendedDare.model` per row certifies X, K and xe together, so rows already taking hewerGain* for K (rv48/rv49 reduced inputs, 28010) add nothing; only rows new to the extended path count against 0.5%.
- Breach lever order: P-solve f, then measured dd Stein residual of Δ̂ (‖P‖₂‖r₂‖ for p(n)eps‖F‖²‖Δ̂‖), never a constant. Still breaching → pay or demote, not waive.
- Care tier 2 does not exist (extendedDare/hewer, Smith doubling, discrete only). Rule Dare now; file "extended Newton–Kleinman, big-float Lyapunov" before any Care gate, else z5a's 122 become WORSE.
- BBN22I: a certified δX gives δK ≤ ‖W⁻¹‖‖B‖‖A‖δX, a derived K resolution to replace gainFloor/gainCap later; out of scope.

## 4. Falsifiers

1. A named or rattle row with f_lo < 1 and P-solve f < 1 from its literals: the noise is elsewhere (gain/W rounding); redo.
2. Extended Hewer at the derived precision disagrees with the 320-bit X by > newtonTol, or fails on an oracle-correct triggered row: precision or model wrong; raise p per the formula first.
3. Any oracle-correct Acc-0 row demoted after the change (expect 0: tier 2 certifies or corrects).
4. Any row certified by tier 1 with X beyond the census band: bound unsound (p(n), κ(E), K term, quad, or the P estimate); must be 0.
5. Any set > 0.5% rows > 2× once the trigger fires: population too large; escalate the lever order.
6. Many f ≥ 1 rows whose float64 step tracks the oracle error within 2×: loose for cost only; motivates the r₂ estimator.

title: DESIGN: LS c2d stiff-descriptor path (pencil target cost, redundant-pole order, Accuracy surface, fracdelay order)
body:
DESIGN for the LS c2d stiff-descriptor path as a whole (target, detector, accuracy surface, order). Filed per the coordinator's pre-launch ruling, after 6QU2G3 r3 parked under its hard stop.

## Starting point
Branch parked/lsfit-wave56-r3 @ 117b7aa (on d638061), with 3 commits:
- 775db84: pencil EvalFr target, f0c5233 integrator detection on parts[0], split cached in the plan, seed-68 guard, FitOrder doc.
- a28d9d2: LeastSquaresFit.Accuracy (C2DFit only), set by the 3-way Ud/Uc detector.
  - ss.go nonStablePoleCount: Ud from the poles IsStable computes.
  - Uc from parts[0] by path (i), quasi-triangular readout, on 889/889 native and 887/887 amd64 routed rows; (iii) fallback.
- 117b7aa: tests.

## What passes (both arches)
- Value is bit-identical to 775db84 (demotion only).
- Non-routed rows are bit-identical to base; 0 value->error.
- Accuracy == [Ud>Uc] against independent oracles; 0 Ud<Uc rows at auto order.
- Every S->U-by-IsStable row is at Accuracy 1. The exception is native ns1600 68: Ud=Uc=1, and the branch's unstable pole 1.13658 is correct for plant +1.415.
- Guards 296, 71 and 68 pass.
- An independent 2000-row sweep per arch agrees.
- Fit error vs the exact twin: branch median 0.0075 vs base 0.052 native, 0.0061 vs 0.054 amd64.

Fires, split by base status:
- census: native 313 (258 already unstable at base, 55 new); amd64 264 (229 / 35);
- sweep: native 88 (74 / 14); amd64 91 (86 / 5).

## Why it parked: PERF (CEFUJP bar), native ns1600
Base-correct rows more than 2x slower: 11/1599 (fixer) or 12/1599 (reviewer), i.e. 0.69-0.75% against a 0.5% limit.
- Rows: ns1600 plain/iodelay/pathdelay 253 (2.12-2.14x), plain/iodelay/pathdelay/scaled7 991 (2.03-2.05x), iodelay 1324 (2.01x), scaled7 191/233/1357 (2.00-2.06x).
- ns400 is 1/421 (scaled7 43, 2.004x). amd64 is 0 in every set.
- Routed native median 0.91x, p90 1.55x, max 2.14x. Ratios cluster at 2.0-2.2x.
- The cause is the 775db84 pencil-response target, not the detector: 775db84 vs 117b7aa gives 0 rows >2x, median 0.996x.
- Generator: nearSingularEDraw (descriptor_e_rank_test.go). The census harness and generators are inlined in 6QU2G3 under "r3 pre-code probe".

## Open design questions
1. Target cost: make pencil EvalFr cheaper on 513-sample grids (reuse the split and Schur form across frequencies), or route only when the fold is predicted inaccurate.
2. Order: auto = n leaves an undetermined redundant near-cancelling pole (54/103/1281/123x7 flip side by rounding). MATLAB's remedy is FitOrder; is a documented-only remedy enough?
3. Accuracy surface: C2D gives no signal (MATLAB parity). C2DFit Accuracy does not fire when Ud<Uc at a user-reduced FitOrder: at order 1, 26 native / 29 amd64 routed rows have Ud<Uc, 14 of them dropping an unstable plant pole. Should Ud<Uc be reported?
4. Fracdelay error rows on routed stiff descriptors pay for foldInaccurateParts before the integer-delay check rejects them (about 2.1x, identical error). Reordering is not pure, so redesign it.
5. LPEXWJ (positive stiff pole), related.

Evidence (scratchpad, not durable): w56review/lsfit/{r7fix,r8rev,r6rev,r3q}.

## Cross-ref 2026-10-30
T73RLU (DESIGN: PolesDetail sound Accuracy) re-filed under this design family per I5CXGD ruling 4; rule the Accuracy surfaces together.

title: CORE: least-squares C2D/C2DFit of stiff descriptors stays on the LU fold; needs a fit-quality decision
body:
conversion_plan.go skips the stiff-parts route for C2DMethodLeastSquares, which goes through conversionStandardForm -> ToExplicit, so E^-1 A is folded with or without delays. Routing it through the parallel pencil parts is not a fix: in wave 45 that made the fit much worse on cont seeds 50, 162, 194, 283 and 334. This needs a decision on what the LS fit should match (the pencil response at the fit frequencies?) before any routing change. Ask the advisor first.
Probe: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-josephj-workspace-controlsys/90f6527f-00fa-4f22-8ebb-64f8a65942a3/scratchpad/w45review/keep/fix_azumsc_ls_probe_test.go.txt (nearSingularEDraw seeds 0..400, routed SISO, fit error vs pencilResponse). Files: conversion_least_squares.go (leastSquaresFit), conversion_plan.go.

## Decision step (advisor, wave 55)
Ruling: the least-squares fit target at the fit frequencies is the descriptor's own frequency response, EvalFr of the pencil (sE-A)^-1, not the folded E^-1 A. MATLAB LS c2d fits the continuous frequency response. The fit algorithm and the discrete explicit realization stay as they are.
DON'T REPEAT: the wave-45 regression (seeds 50/162/194/283/334) came from discretizing by parallel parts, which is a different change.
Dump (wave 55): rerun the probe on main (nearSingularEDraw 0..400, fit error vs pencilResponse). This sizes the class and gives the base numbers the bar will cite. If the base fit error vs the pencil is already small on most rows, the task is narrower than its title.

## Wave-55 dump result: READY, narrower than the title
- The class is small: 40 of 401 draws (295 are skipped as rank-deficient E, 64 as m != 1).
- On main the routed LS fit is identical to the fold's LS fit. The pencil response matches the exact twin to 1e-15.
- Fit vs pencil: median 0.060, max 0.967, 39/40 > 1e-3. The fold-vs-pencil response gap is median 3.7%, max 22% (seeds 296, 71, 59, 171, 116, 355...). The LS fit of the EXACT TWIN already misses by a median of 2.8%, so the method's own error dominates most rows.
- BAR (constant-free, relative): on every row, the fit-vs-pencil error <= the exact twin's own LS fit error. Direction unchanged: the pencil EvalFr is the target and the algorithm stays the same.
- Check the probe's frequency grid against Nyquist before treating the 2.8% method error as a defect. If it persists below fs/2, that is a separate task, not folded in here.
Evidence: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-josephj-workspace-controlsys/90f6527f-00fa-4f22-8ebb-64f8a65942a3/scratchpad/w55dec/3PWI4Q/ (native_summary.txt, native.jsonl, zz_3pwi4q_test.go).

## Wave-56 result + ruling (advisor, recorded before round 3)
Branch fix/lsfit-wave56 @ a406dc0 (c11aaa6 target = pencil EvalFr, routed LS only; a406dc0 doc). Partial: (1) single-run twin-own bar is noise (orthogonal state change moves it 2x median, 741x max); (2) spurious integrator on stiff rows: leastSquaresIntegratorLimit tol 1e-10*||A||_1 with ||A||~1e15 -> k=1 with no pole near 0, seeds 43/71/296/344 (PCG(seed,7704)); c11aaa6 REGRESSES 296 0.222->0.541 and 71 0.491->0.515 native; (3) redundant pole: auto order n while minimal order n-1, pole lands on rounding near z=+-1 (seed 54 pole -1.35316 / zero -1.35359).
RULING:
1. ACCEPT departure "integrator-detection-on-slow-part": integrator count/residue from the explicit parts foldInaccurateParts already returns, routed-descriptor LS rows only, same gate as target change; existing tolerance on the right matrix, no new constant; detection only, not discretization by parts (not wave-45). Prototype /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-josephj-workspace-controlsys/90f6527f-00fa-4f22-8ebb-64f8a65942a3/scratchpad/w56review/lsfit/p1_prototype_with_target.diff (43 0.191->0.0076, 71 ->0.028, 296 ->0.110, 344 0.967->0.083).
2. REJECT slow-order auto (reviewer P1/P2, /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-josephj-workspace-controlsys/90f6527f-00fa-4f22-8ebb-64f8a65942a3/scratchpad/w56review/lsfit/r3fix/proto_slow_order.diff): MATLAB auto = continuous order; 7/40 rows worse up to 23.6x; P2 stabilises unstable plants.
3. BAR REWORDED: branch fit-vs-pencil error within the N-draw rounding band of the same LS routine fitting the PENCIL target (not twin ToExplicit().EvalFr: omega=0 bug). N=30 draws, 1e-15 relative target noise, rng PCG(seed,9001). Rows outside band listed by seed with ratio; coordinator rules each.
4. STABILITY: flips at |z|=1 within rounding not counted. Count only base-stable rows where branch max|z| exceeds the band's own pole spread. Seed 54 is the known such row; if it persists under the integrator fix, explicit exception referencing the redundant-pole task; no fit-order change here.
5. Other bars unchanged: non-routed/explicit/wellE LS + other methods bit-identical, 0 value->error, perf CEFUJP, native AND amd64, full 40-row (ns400) and ns1600 sets; recompute band numbers under the integrator fix (twin fold also hit it).

## Round 3 GRANT (coordinator, advisor-reviewed) - HARD STOP, supersedes ruling items 3-4 above
Scope: EXACTLY departure (1) integrator-detection-on-slow-part (foldInaccurateParts slow part, same routed-LS gate, no new constant). Slow-order auto (2) stays rejected. Then one full probe rerun.
BAR:
- Band: for each routed row, 30 draws of 1e-15 relative noise on the pencil target, rng PCG(seed,9001), same LS routine -> [min,max] of fit-vs-pencil error. ## Wave 26 review (2026-10-25): BLOCKED; branch fix/descriptor-wave26 kept
- BLOCKING: f459b00 (capped sampleBand/bandCeil + errPolyUnseen + weierstrassReduceSplits accepting a splitQZStatic proper re-split when polySamplesMismatch <= 1 in the capped band): genuinely improper models with small s-terms beside a large-A pole now read IsProper=true and get a proper TF that is wrong at data-determined points. Others now fail closed (errPolyUnseen, ErrDescriptorSingular) where base returned the correct improper TF. The capped band excludes the |s| range where small s-terms are visible, so polyVisible is false, errPolyUnseen fires, and the static proper re-split is accepted against those same samples. This violates the owner rules 'improper must return IsProper=false (MATLAB isproper)' and 'IsProper/Step/TF agree with truth'.

The chain kernel-state b is Gaussian and the other chain-state b entries are Gaussian times bscale. Oracle: the structured (F,W,b,c,D) pencil.

Key case, bscale 1e-6, seed 5 (poles -0.0958, 6697.16, 0.569):
- Base: IsProper=false; the improper TF matches the oracle to 2.1e-11 at 0.5+3i and 7.7e-9 at 1e2i.
- Branch: IsProper=true, Step nil, proper TF off by 2.2e-6 at 0.5+3i, where the stored data determine the response to 3.6e-11. It is also off by 6.0e-2 at 1e2i (data-determined to 5.5e-7).
- Over 5 copies with 4-eps jitter, base is correct 5/5 and branch wrong 5/5.
- Seed 138: branch off by 2.8e-5 at 0.5+3i (data-determined to 1.4e-10) and 1.04 at 1e2i.

Counts per 150 draws:
- improper read proper on the branch, bscale 1e-6: 15 native, 10 amd64 (base: 2 and 2).
- improper read proper on the branch, bscale 1e-8: 34 native, 32 amd64 (base: 2 and 4). At 1e-8 the TF is often within data uncertainty and only IsProper flips.
- value->error where base was robust-correct (5/5 jitter): native bscale 1e-4 seeds 9, 33, 60, 114; bscale 1e-6 seeds 9, 37, 108, 122, 148. Example: gen0 1e-4 seed 9 base improper TF 4.8e-13 off; branch 'IsProper: s-terms of a recounted split not seen in direct pencil solves'.
- In total, 42 base-robust-correct cases go wrongprop or closed on the branch natively. The amd64 extra sweep shows the same pattern (53 REGRESS lines).

Bisect (detail probe on seeds 5 and 33 at 1e-6 and seed 9 at 1e-4): 4491e78, 9d05825 and d2c8c4f are correct (IsProper=false with TF). f459b00 and 6238217 give IsProper=true, or errPolyUnseen for seed 9.
- BLOCKING: 4491e78 (eigdecomp leakCarried/ambiguousAboveLeak plus qzFiniteMatch in generalizedPoles): Poles() drops the true finite pole that is large in A, beside an index>=2 chain. deflateInfinite now succeeds with nf one short, so the large pole is counted as infinite. On refuted seed 460 natively this turns IsStable from false (correct: pole +93147) to true. Poles is a public value regression. It can also return an empty slice with a nil error for a model that has a finite pole, and it disagrees with a correct TF.

Branch Poles = {-0.19647, -0.21008}, IsStable=true (wrong). Over 5 copies with 4-eps jitter, base IsStable is correct 4/5 and branch wrong 4/5.

- refuted 417 native: IsProper=true with a matching TF, but Poles has 4 values with pole error 0.97.

FABLE RULING (coordinator-adopted, 2026-11-12). Shared mechanism: leave the float rank decisions alone and certify the reduced object a-posteriori against the stored model, in two tiers. title: EDGE: AbsorbIO: keep non-decomposable residual as shared internal delays (minimality improvement; AY2CYR closed)
body:
Found in wave 17 (fix/wave17). AY2CYR partial merged (58fbbe4 tie-break). Remaining duplication argued structural; MATLAB has no IO-only absorb target.

[w17 #69 edges] AY2CYR: decide between (a) closing as partial / won't-fix, since one copy of the internal delays per piece is structural and MATLAB has no IO-only absorb to match, and (b) a new task to keep the non-decomposable residual as shared internal delays with the decomposable input and output delays absorbed as states. For the test plant (b) gives n=4, q=4, against today's n=7, q=4. Both are AbsorbIO in delay_residual_split.go.

[w17 #73 edges] AY2CYR reproduced. With n=1, m=3, p=2, a non-decomposable SetDelay, OutputDelay set, and 2 internal LFT delays: continuous AbsorbDelay(AbsorbIO) gives q=4 (2 column pieces) and discrete gives q=6 (3 column pieces). The response still matches the original. In the general case this cannot be soundly fixed:
(1) The duplication is structural, not a copying bug. Each split piece is out_g * G * in_g. A diagonal output delay does not commute with a non-diagonal G, so every group needs its own copy of the states, and the internal-delay loop (B2/C2/D22, Tau) goes with each copy. Sharing Tau channels across pieces would give a wrong model.
(2) For discrete AbsorbIO, the existing per-group cost (n + sum of in/out delay samples) is exactly the realized state count, so the base already picks the split with the fewest states. Weighting internal delays in the cost only trades states for channels. I tried it: discrete repro went 27 states/6 channels -> 33/4, with neither dominating, so I reverted it.
(3) MATLAB parity sets no achievable target. MATLAB ss has no IODelay matrix: a non-decomposable IODelay already becomes InternalDelay at construction, so "MATLAB keeps the original internal delays" describes a different model. It is not something this absorption path can match.
Delivered the one strictly better change (commit 58fbbe4, branch fix/edges-wave17, delay_residual_split.go newResidualDelaySplit). When row and column costs tie and the model has internal delays, pick the split with fewer pieces. Same state count, fewer duplicated internal-delay channels. q=0 behaviour is unchanged. Example: Delay [[3,1,0],[1,0,0]], dt=1, n=1, internal Tau [3,2]. AbsorbIO goes from 7 states/6 internal delays to 7/4. PullDelaysToLFT goes from 3 states/9 delays to 2/7. The original repro (no tie) is unchanged. A model with redundant internal delays is still correct; it is just not minimal.

[w17 #74 edges] QFAIOB is fixed (commit 91bca71 on fix/edges-wave17). AY2CYR reproduces but I left it alone: it needs a coordinator decision.

QFAIOB: I reproduced the bug. With A at scale 1e298 or 1e-300, 5 of the 6 points just off a real pole (all but λ≈-6.7e297) gave EvalFr = NaN with a nil error, while ddResponseInto had the right finite value. The fix is in /Users/josephj/workspace/controlsys/.claude/worktrees/wf_b27620d1-19f-28/frequency_hessenberg.go. A new helper, finiteResponse(dst), now runs at the end of both balancedDense.evalInto and hessenbergSweep.evalInto. If any output entry is NaN or Inf it returns errSingularPencil, which is not errNonFinitePencil, so evalWithPoleLimitGated goes on to the ddResponseInto / pole-limit fallback. All 6 repro points now match ddResponseInto. That includes the reviewer's case (b) at sc=1e-300, where base gave a wrong -2.0.

New test: TestEvalFrExtremeScaleNearPole in frequency_graded_test.go. The oracle is exact scale invariance: scaling A and B by a power of two (2^990 and 2^-996), and s by the same factor, leaves the response unchanged, so the unit-scale model gives the reference value. It checks EvalFr and both solvers through evalWithPoleLimit at s=λ(1-1e-10) for each real eigenvalue, with relative tolerance 1e-5. With the source change removed the test fails with NaN on 15 checks.

Benchmarks (benchcmp, base 7c14e32 against the working tree): +2.4% geomean, worst +5.8% (FreqResponseWithDelay), no extra allocations. Nothing near a 2x slowdown.

AY2CYR (not fixed, coordinator decision needed): it reproduces as described, q=4 against the reviewer's target of 2. I think the duplication is structural. The response is y = Σ_g Dout_g·H12·K·H21·Din_g·u_g, where K = Δ(I−H22Δ)⁻¹ is the internal-delay loop. The output delays Dout_g differ from piece to piece, and a single shared K loses which piece its output belongs to. So any realization that turns IO delays into states needs one copy of K per piece. The "MATLAB 2" target is also not something MATLAB does: MATLAB stores a non-decomposable ioDelay on an ss model as internal delays, and its absorbDelay on a discrete model absorbs every delay, internal ones included. There is no IO-only absorb mode to match.

For this test plant (total delay [[4,2,1],[1,0,0]], dt=1), the reviewer's alternative works out like this. The best split is input delay [1,0,0] plus output delay [1,0], leaving 2 residual entries ([2,1,0] on output 1). Absorbing the input and output delays as shifts and keepin


## Decision (advisor, 2026-10-22)
Close AY2CYR as done. The duplication is non-minimality by construction: the delay loop must travel with each non-commuting piece, the response matches, and MATLAB has no IO-only absorb. Option (b), shared internal delays, is filed as an EDGE improvement.

body:

- **Bug:** AllMargin places gain crossovers within about 1e-13 of a DC pole wrongly, and sometimes reports spurious ones.
- **Repro:** the dover-grid and dover-pcg rows in c3:

title: EDGE: zeros rankMargin reports +Inf for rank-0 colPivotQR rejection; inflated margins in prescaledStaircaseZeros
body:
Found in wave 19 (fix/wave19). JHFQWK residual (left unfixed: widens comparison path, needs its own sweep).

[w19 #28 tfzeros/fix] rankMargin under-reports how close a rank-0 rejection came to its threshold. colPivotQR returns sval=[rejected,0,0] when rank is 0, so rankMargin (zeros.go) sees sv[2]=0 and returns +Inf for that decision. Repro: the JHFQWK model (TestZerosVanishingMarkovInfinite data), D=0; reduceStaircase(sys).margin reports 3.7e11. The rejected QR values in that reduction were actually 2.1e-16, 1.7e-15, 1.7e-14 and 2.2e-14 against a threshold of 2.9e-13, so the true margins were about 13 to 1400. Effect: the low and preferRaw decisions in prescaledStaircaseZeros see inflated margins for the unscaled reduction. Files: zeros.go (rankMargin, zerosStaircasePass), qr_colpivot.go. This was not fixed because it widens the comparison path and needs its own sweep.

## Probe; no code; needs design
Real: qr_colpivot.go:143-146 zeroes sminpr at rank 0; rankMargin +Inf. Deleting it: JHFQWK D=0 raw margin 3.748e11 -> 13.34. But ZerosDetail 8000 rows, one shard, value<->error 0: arm64 right->wrong 20, wrong->right 1; amd64 23, 3. Raw only 10,1; balanced only 11,3. Lower margins send more models into arbitration or flip its tie-break (0:1964 gains -1.5e14; 0:3305 loses 2 zeros). rankMarginMin, rankMarginTrust tuned on inflated margins (inferred). Options: close as known with a comment; diagnostic-only margin; rework arbitration as its own task. Oracle coarse: zeros by construction, 1e-3; amd64 rows not inspected. Harness: worker scratchpad 7mp62g.


KF4VME: this probe harness is noisy; its right->wrong counts carry ~79% noise. Remeasure with kf4vme oracle before any ruling. Path 2 arbitration picks wrong reduction 15/57 sampled.

title: CORE: discrete AllMargin misses |L|=1 crossover with nil when at(0) mis-evaluates near DC pole (ref CWMCXC)
body:
Found by the CWMCXC fixer (2026-11-12). Pre-existing and critical: a wrong result with nil.
- **Bug:** discrete AllMargin misses the |L|=1 gain crossover and returns a nil error.
- **Repro:** the d-row models at p=1e-305 and 1e-307 (literals discrete1e-305/discrete1e-307 in margin_bandwidth_scan_floor_test.go on branch CWMCXC). The model is Dt=1, A=[1, 2p; p/2, 1], B=[1, 0.5], C=[0.7e-10·p·1e300, −0.2e-10·p·1e300], D=0.01. AllMargin returns GainCrossFreqs=[] with nil; the oracle values are 6.0002999985688122e-16 and 6.0002999244552604e-18.
- **Evidence:**
  - At p=1e-305 the double at(0) returns 0.010000000109999997 (about D) with ok=true, while the true |L(0)| is about 6e289.
  - gainCandidates(1) is empty, and the sign at DC matches the sign at pLo, so no scan runs.
  - At p=1e-302, at(0) snaps to +Inf and the pencil finds the root.
  - Bandwidth handles these rows only because bandwidth() sets eval.exact when try(0) < gamma; allMargin has no equivalent.
- **Files:** margin.go allMargin/gainCrossings; the pole-limit gate in sisoEval.at.
- **Also check (not reproduced):** a discrete crossing within one ulp of Nyquist. The top-end scan stops when wTop−t == wTop and drops it.
- **Cross-ref:** CWMCXC, RLCKVA.

RULING (coordinator, 2026-11-12): APPROVED next after CWMCXC. Widen the scope check first: check whether the public EvalFr/FreqResponse at ω=0 (discrete z=1) also returns ≈D with nil on the repro. If it does, the fix belongs in the evaluator under the same NSYMIV disk rule: a pole within its own rounding disk of z=1 → Inf/limit, else exact or ErrAccuracyUnverified. A2OX65 then covers it, and AllMargin must not paper over it with eval.exact. Include the near-Nyquist one-ulp check.

## Scope check (fixer, 2026-11-12): the public evaluator is wrong; HELD for a ruling
- **Wrong values:** the discrete repro at p=1e-305 and 1e-307 gives FreqResponse/EvalFr at ω=0 and 1e-300 ≈ D (0.0100000001…) with nil. The oracle |G| is 6e289. DCGain certifies −6e289.
- **Nearby frequencies:** at ω 1e-20 and 1e-16 the result is errPoleUnresolved (honest). At 1e-14 it is correct. At p=1e-302 it is +Inf.
- **Cause:** the NSYMIV disk rule (1a8b496, originResponseInto) correctly takes the pole-limit path, since the poles sit inside their 2.2e-16 disk of z=1. poleLimitInto's residue test (poleResidueTol·|δ·g| ≈ 1e-13) then reads the exact residue 6e-16 as rounding and extrapolates to ≈D. The literal rule does not fix it.
- **Options:** (a) change the poleLimitInto residue classification, which is shared by all callers; (b) return ErrAccuracyUnverified when the limit is finite but a computed pole sits inside its disk of DC; (c) other.
- **AllMargin:** the missed crossover 6e-16 is about 3× the disk, so it may count as unresolved rather than missed.
- **Near-Nyquist:** q ≥ 1e-16 is fine (1–3 ulp). At q ≤ 1e-17 the true crossing lies between float π and true π, and Bandwidth gives +Inf with nil. Semantics call: +Inf over float ω, or Nyquist / unv.
- **Probes:** scratchpad/a2ox65/zz_a2_scope*_test.go.

RULING (coordinator, 2026-11-12): HOLD for Fable on the residue rule. poleResidueTol is a tuned constant, and the (b) path risks WORSE on genuinely cancelled pole/zero pairs inside the disk (the W45MGH family); Fable is asked for a derived residue bound and the AllMargin consequence. Near-Nyquist RULED: +Inf judged over float ω up to π/Dt (the float Nyquist). Add a doc line on Bandwidth: "frequencies are the float64 values up to π/Dt; a crossing between float π/Dt and the exact Nyquist is not reported" (MATLAB also evaluates up to pi/Ts in floating point). Freeze q≤1e-17 as a literal documenting it; it can ride with A2OX65.

## RULING (Fable, coordinator-adopted, 2026-11-12)

### Decision
**(a).** Replace poleResidueTol in poleLimitInto with a derived bound.

**(b) is REJECTED as a rule.** Every channel with exactly zero cluster residue would go finite-nil-correct → unv, which is WORSE, and it doesn't produce the ruled answer. Such channels include MIMO channels the integrator doesn't reach, block-triangular realizations, and the W45MGH family.

### Residue test, per channel
pole ⇔ r̂_j > B_round,j + B_trunc,j, where r̂ estimates the cluster's total residue C·P_cl·B.
- Use the 5-point binomial residue formula w = 5δ(1,−4,6,−4,1), unconditionally. The 3-point formula fails truncation on the repro.
- B_trunc = 1920·M·(δ/ρ)⁴·δ, with M ≤ |D_ij| + 2Σ_{k∉cl}|r_k|/ρ (Cauchy).
- B_round = Σ|w_k|·e_k, where e_k is the componentwise γ₃ₙ forward-error bound of sample k. The normwise form from poleSpacing/poleEigen data is acceptable.
- r̂ > B → Inf (Q1-A). r̂ ≤ B → finite extrapolation.

### Step 2 (CEFUJP-gated)
Applies on the finite branch when n≤16 and a pole sits inside its disk of dc.
- Evaluate ddResponse at dc; if dd is singular or underflows, use exact.
- det=0 → integrator; the classification stands.
- Exact value within bound(f̂) → return it, nil.
- Otherwise → Inf.
- Never unv here.

### AllMargin / Bandwidth
- When a sign change between DC and the first evaluable ω gives a bracket that can't close on evaluable ω, return ErrAccuracyUnverified, never [] nil (that would be a nonexistence claim).
- Points below the resolution floor must read +Inf with a consistent sign.
- errPoleUnresolved must not make scan silently drop the bracket.
- eval.exact is not the fix.

### Expected repro outcomes
- p=1e-305 AllMargin → [6.0003e-16] nil (certified).
- p=1e-307 AllMargin → unv.
- Bandwidth on both → unv (the −3 dB crossing is inside the disk).
- FreqResponse at ω∈{0, 1e-300} → Inf nil; ω=1e-14 unchanged.

### Near-Nyquist (CORRECTS the earlier ruling)
+Inf with nil is a nonexistence claim. When the crossing lies between fl(π) and π:
- return fl(π)/Dt, nil, if nyquistResponse certifies the response is below threshold there;
- otherwise return unv.

Freeze the q≤1e-17 literal under this rule. The earlier doc line is DROPPED.

### F3, a new exposure: rule it before merge
With (a), FreqResponse at s≠dc inside a pole's disk could flip from errPoleUnresolved to Inf nil on the repro. At 1e-16, |G|=6 is resolved by dd; at 1e-20, |G|=6e4.
- RULING: a resolved dd value stands at s≠dc.
- ddAtPole may demote to an error but never promote to Inf.
- Count the affected census points.

### Measure first
- **F1:** |r̂_double − r̂_dd| ≤ B everywhere on census DC pole-limit rows.
- **F2:** every finite→Inf flip must be oracle-Inf, or in-disk with a nonzero oracle residue. One oracle-finite flip means the bound is too tight; stop.
- **F3:** count of affected points, as above.
- **F4:** the repro outcomes above.
- **F5:** CEFUJP on band-F5/ls-modal.

### Placement
After CWMCXC in the non-Riccati queue. Light work until the timing gaps. JW5H7V stage 1 and A2OX65 can both be implemented as light work, but their censuses run one at a time.

## SNAP-GATE RULINGS (coordinator, 2026-11-12)

The proposal is ADOPTED: it is derived, and it is the F3 rule applied to the margin gate.
- Resolution floor = the dc rounding disk: the largest first-order move ε·|y|ᵀ|A||x|/|yᴴx| among poles inside their own move, from eigenvalueRoundingTerms.
- Inside the disk: +Inf with a consistent sign.
- Between the disk and `near`: the resolved dd value stands, replacing the snap.
- NOTE: poleStepFraction (1e-5 band) is a tuned constant, now demoted to a perf gate. It no longer decides values.
- Census-watch every margin and PID consumer beside an integrator or a z=1 cluster.

### 1. CWMCXC d* rows (discrete 1e-302, 1e-305, 1e-307)
Don't flip them blindly. Base is main, where these return +Inf nil (wrong), so neither outcome is WORSE. The rule is still to prefer a certified value over unv.
- If CWMCXC's scaled-evaluator value at those crossings comes from a path with a real certificate (state which bound, at which ω), it stays nil, and Fable's "unv" expectation is amended for that row.
- If the only support is agreement with the oracle, flip it to unv in the A2OX65 commit, with oracle numbers in the test comment.
- Run CWMCXC's census after A2OX65 lands, or re-read its d* rows then.
- 1e-302 follows the same test.

### 2. Bracket rule
A sign change between a determined DC sign (+Inf inside the disk counts as determined) and the first evaluable point means a crossing EXISTS. Silently dropping it was wrong-with-nil, not correct. Read the census first:
- any row going base nil → unv where the oracle says NO crossing exists → stop and report; that's a sign-determination bug;
- rows where the oracle confirms a crossing → honest.

### 3. Scope
Scoping (a) to explicit delay-free models is OK. State the counts of descriptor and internal-delay rows that keep the old rule. A CORE follow-up is filed so the tuned constant has an owner.

## Implementation stop (2026-11-12, WIP 86a5fd6 on CWMCXC 6bee169): the ruled B_round is too loose
- **F4:** all repro outcomes are as ruled.
  - p=1e-305 AllMargin = 6.00029999856881e-16 nil; p=1e-307 unv; Bandwidth unv on both; FreqResponse at 0 and 1e-300 is Inf.
  - Near-Nyquist q≤1e-17 → fl(π) nil, certified.
  - CWMCXC d* rows → unv (dd support only, no certificate).
- **F1 holds:** |r̂_d − r̂_dd| ≤ B.
- **Failure:** the first-order γ₃ₙ forward bound B_round exceeds r̂ by 10¹–10²³ on genuine poles, because z_kI−A is near-singular next to a cluster and the error lies along the null direction. Examples:

  | case | r̂ | B_round |
  |---|---|---|
  | s²(s+1)(s+1e-9) | 2.28e23 | 5.05e46 |
  | (z−1)³ | 3.81e8 | 2.55e10 |
  | stiff integrator family | 1.86 | 2.19 |
  | off-DC resonance | 8.3e-5 | 1.8e6 |

- **Targeted tests:**
  - Inf→finite (WORSE): DCGainRoundedStiffIntegratorFamily, DCGainFreqResponseAtDCConsistency, FreqResponseAtPoleExplicitAndDescriptor, PoleLimitOriginClusterNoWindow (−6.8e25 nil), PoleLimitSamplesBesideOriginCluster.
  - New nil-wrong: SISOEvalAtOffDCPoleLimitUnverified.
  - New unv: several AllMargin unit-cluster tests.
- **Options:**
  - (1) a relative bound γ·cond(eigvec)·|r̂| for the cluster part plus a forward bound on the rest;
  - (2) a-posteriori B_round from dd samples, c·|r̂_d − r̂_dd| + dd noise (F1 shows it is tight);
  - (3) the derived test only for simple well-separated clusters, legacy otherwise.
  - Fixer lean: (2) for n≤16, (3) above.
- **Data:** probes in scratchpad/a2ox65/.

## B_round RULING (Fable, coordinator-adopted, 2026-11-12)

The forward bound on the samples is the wrong object. Use a STRUCTURED bound: |r̂ − R| ≤ Θ|R| + B_abs.

**Setup**
- Split M_k⁻¹ into the cluster-projector part P (bounded relatively) and the regular part Q (bounded absolutely).
- q=1: θ_k = c_k/(kδ) + μ + ν_k, where:
  - c_k = γρ_g|y|ᵀ(|A|+|z_k|I)|x|/|yᴴx| (the pole's rounding disk);
  - μ = γ(|y|ᵀ|B|/|yᴴB| + |C||x|/|Cx|);
  - ν_k = ‖E_k‖‖QM_k⁻¹Q‖(‖y‖‖B‖/|yᴴB| + ‖C‖‖x‖/|Cx|).
- Θ = Σ_k(|w_k|/(kδ))·θ_k/(1−θ_k), with the 5-point weights; valid iff θ_k<1.
- B_abs = B_trunc + Σ|w_k|E_reg,k, with E_reg,k = γρ_g‖C‖‖B‖κ_Q²‖M_k‖/ρ_k² + 2γ‖C‖‖B‖κ_Q/ρ_k + γ|D|, and ρ_k = dist(z_k, Λ_reg).
- q>1: use the cluster Schur block T_cl (originPoleCluster already forms it), with θ_k = ‖(z_k−T_cl)⁻¹‖·‖E_k‖.

**Test**
- POLE ⇔ r̂ > B_abs and Θ<1 → Inf.
- FINITE ⇔ r̂ ≤ B_abs, Θ<1, AND the 5-point and 3-point extrapolants agree within their own bounds.
- Θ≥1, or the extrapolants disagree → recompute the samples in dd under the SAME bound with dd constants. If still undecided → ErrAccuracyUnverified. Never Inf, never finite.
- Option (2), the |r̂_d − r̂_dd| difference, is NOT a certificate. It is falsifier F1 only.

**Scope**
- No legacy branch for explicit/descriptor models at any n.
- One Schur factorization per sys, cached. exactDetMaxOrder caps only the optional exact confirm.

**Internal-delay LFT path**
- Apply the unstructured normwise bound on the dd LFT samples: r̂ above it → Inf, below → unv. Census-count those rows.
- If base-nil-correct LFT rows go unv: keep poleResidueTol for the LFT path ONLY (renamed, documented as tuned), and file a CORE task for an LFT-structured derivation.

**Other items**
- SISOEvalAtOffDCPoleLimitUnverified: at s≠dc the resolved dd value stands. Demote only, never promote to Inf.
- AllMargin unit-cluster unv: the bracket rule applies only when DC reads Inf (or certified >γ) AND the first evaluable point is on the other side. A certified finite DC with no sign change is no bracket, so no unv.
- The 5 flipped tests must return to Inf (Θ≪1 and r̂≫B_abs on all of them).

**Falsifiers, in order**
- F1: |r̂_d − r̂_dd| ≤ Θ|r̂_dd| + B_abs on every pole-limit evaluation.
- F2: every classification change is oracle-checked.
- F3: Θ≥1 rates in double and in dd. List the unv rows with their base state; nil-correct → WORSE.
- F4: extrapolant-disagreement count, oracle-checked.
- F5: CEFUJP, including the factorization cost.

**Light work.** The census stays queued after RLCKVA.

## Structured-bound implementation stop (2026-11-13, WIP da0facf): held for a ruling
- **F4:** all repro outcomes are as ruled. **F1** holds.
- **Escape hatch taken:** the LFT path keeps a renamed tuned lftPoleResidueTol/lftPoleResidueFloor. A follow-up CORE task is filed.
- **New departure:** descriptor models are reduced by E⁻¹ when κ(E)·ε < 1e-3. The 1e-3 is a new constant and needs a ruling.
- **STOP 1 (bracket):** TestAllMarginPhaseCrossDelayedUnitCluster ring6/7 goes nil→unv where the oracle has no crossing. The ring poles lie inside their first-order disk (about 1.7e-3), so the gain search reads +Inf at DC while the evaluator resolves |L|≈0.39. TestAllMarginGainCrossUnitClusterSweep goes nil-correct → unv (WORSE).
- **STOP 2 (vacuous FINITE, nil-wrong):** when B_abs is huge (4.2e26, 3.7e16), r̂≤B_abs holds trivially. The projector split is ill-conditioned (‖X‖ 2.5e10 / 2.6e7). Affected: TestSISOEvalAtOffDCPoleLimitUnverified, TestDCGainFreqResponseAtDCConsistency.
- **Θ≥1 in dd too:** PoleLimitOriginClusterNoWindow and s²(s+1)(s+1e-9) give unv where Inf is expected.
- **Undiagnosed Inf→finite:** DCGainRoundedStiffIntegratorFamily seeds 20/21/25/28/31, and FreqResponseAtPoleExplicitAndDescriptor discrete.
- **Decisions needed:**
  - (i) Does the disk +Inf at DC yield to a resolved finite DC on the far side of γ?
  - (ii) What determinacy condition does FINITE need?
  - (iii) How is the cluster defined when ‖X‖ is huge (grow the cluster, or merge into a q≥2 block)?

## ROUND-3 RULING (Fable, coordinator-adopted, 2026-11-13)

### (i) Bracket ends: YES
- An end is (a) an evaluation the solver resolved (double, or dd with ddResponse verification and no ddAtPole veto), or (b) solveDCRegular's CERTIFIED finite DC gain.
- A snapped Inf is never an end. The DC snap is a point-value convention for FreqResponse/DCGain and stays out of the margin search.
- Expected results:
  - ring6/7 → no crossing, nil;
  - UnitClusterSweep → 1.48e-4, nil;
  - repro 1e-305 → bracket [4.4e-16, 1.57e-15], nil;
  - repro 1e-307 → unv.

### (ii) FINITE determinacy: YES
- b₃ = Σ|v_k|E_reg,k + truncation + (Σ|v_k|/(kδ))·(r̂+B_abs)/(1−Θ).
- FINITE nil requires b₃ ≤ τ|f̂|, where τ is the DOCUMENTED pole-limit accuracy (1e-12 simple / 1e-9 repeated). Cite the doc line in the code.
- If no doc states τ: stop and report.
- Otherwise → undecided.

### (iii) Cluster growth: YES
- Order poles by distance from dc, starting with the in-disk set.
- Add the nearest regular pole while the ACTUAL Sylvester solution has ‖Z‖ > 1 (T_cl Z − Z T_reg = −T₁₂).
- Stop at ‖Z‖ ≤ 1 or at the whole spectrum.
- Then recompute δ, q and θ_k = ‖(z_k−T_cl)⁻¹‖‖E_k‖.

### κ(E)ε<1e-3: REJECTED
Either fold Skeel cond(E)·γ into ‖E_k‖ and E_reg,k, or (preferred) run the structured bound on the pencil zE−A directly, with generalized eigenvectors and yᴴEx denominators.

### SPLIT ADOPTED
Certified-only scope (A):
- explicit delay-free;
- point at dc;
- cluster grown to ‖Z‖≤1;
- Θ<1 (double or dd);
- POLE on r̂ > B_abs;

- **DEPARTURE:** every repro has f_lo = 1.3 (BN4LWB class). On the advisor's reading, the eps floor needs no δX certificate, so the bound only rejects and Hewer certifies K with its own instrument. Not coordinator-ruled.
- **Census/CEFUJP:** scripts in scratchpad/bbn22i/, not run; estimated 5–6 h native.
- **Out of scope:** non-rLost red-nil pencil K at dareInputs :1169 has no resolution check (bound only, no repro).

RULING (coordinator clarification, 2026-11-13): option (a) ACCEPTED. The BN4LWB constraint forbids BBN22I's own bound from CERTIFYING K on f_lo ≥ 1 rows. A reject-only gate is the safe direction: certification still comes from Hewer's extended fixed point, the same tier-2 instrument BN4LWB prescribes. Conditions:
- Hewer-certified rows must be bit-identical to base where base already took Hewer.
- Where Hewer can't certify → Accuracy 1, never Acc0.
- The census lists the f_lo ≥ 1 rows that change status separately, each oracle-checked (K vs ≥320-bit). One wrong Acc0 → stop.
- Any base-correct Acc0 row going Acc1 is WORSE.
Census queued after RLCKVA's.

title: DECISION: Dare certified-wrong at Newton noise floor (NFET2G b)
body:
DECISION (Riccati CORE): Dare certified-wrong from the Newton noise floor (split from NFET2G class b)

These rows are still certified-wrong after NFET2G (a):
- native: zrwreg 17961 (Dare, Dlqr), zrwbig 21057, 28511
- amd64: zrwbig 12378, 14201, 27310; zrwreg 26697

Root cause: ‖X‖ is about 1e13–1e15 (a weakly controllable mode). One float64 Newton step taken from the rounded 320-bit X moves it 1.3e-8 to 7e-8, even with a double-double gain. So the step is noise, and the noise floor is above newtonTol. verifyRiccati accepts on a tiny refined step (it>0) or on the first step (it=0, amd64 14201 and 27310), while X is 1.4e-8 to 5.2e-8 off.

Measured gates (full table in the NFET2G PR body; census outputs are in scratchpad/nfet2g/on and oa):
- previous step ≤ newtonTol: rejects genuine quadratic convergence; 13 rv48 demotions, 2 nil→error.
- own step ≤ newtonRefineTol, or ≤ newtonTol: demotes 146 native and 173 amd64 oracle-correct rows, plus nil→error on zrwreg and z5a.
- it=0 smallest-step gate: demotes rv48 575 and others.
The demoted rows' X are 1e-9 to 2e-8 off, the same as the named rows, so step-based gates can't separate them.

Options needing a ruling:
1. An explicit noise-floor estimate, which costs solves on every certified Dare.
2. A resolution-limited X band in the census.
3. A waiver.

Side note: the own-step ≤ newtonTol gate cut z5a Care certified-wrong rows from 17 to 1 native and from 23 to 8 amd64.

FABLE RULING (coordinator-adopted, 2026-11-12), verbatim from bn4lwb-ruling.md (probe ak_probe.py beside it in the coordinator's scratchpad). Coordinator order: (a) measure first, no solver change: harness emits ‖F‖₂, f_lo, f_hi per row on base; trigger population per set against CEFUJP 0.5%; compute f for 17961 and the 2ARMRV rattle rows from literals before assuming class. (b) Dare only; Care gate waits for the Care tier-2 task. (c) Falsifiers: any hit → stop and report. BN4LWB and 2ARMRV run as one task, measure phase first; Riccati slot after BBN22I.
# BN4LWB ruling: Dare X certificate at the Newton noise floor

## Decision

Option 1 with a derived trigger; the existing extended-precision Hewer (`hewerSolution`) is the second instrument. Reject 2 and 3.

- Reject 2: the census band `max(newtonTol, 4·sx)` already is the derived data-resolution band, and the named rows exceed it: zrwreg 17961 ex 1.70e-8 vs sx 5.07e-10 (33×), 26697 ex 1.56e-8 vs sx 1.65e-10 (94×). The data determines X to ~1e-9; the float64 instrument cannot. A band that scales with cond would certify 17961 at 2e-9 and still be 1.7e-8 wrong.
- Reject 3: a wrong value under nil breaks the error contract.
- The 146–173 demoted rows pass the same band: correct X, invalid certificate. The fix re-certifies them with a valid instrument; the problem is tier-2 cost, not demotion.

## 1. Certificate, and why no float64 step separates the rows

Δ is a float64 Bartels–Stewart solve of the Stein equation in F = E⁻¹(A − BK). Backward error p(n)·eps·‖F‖² through L⁻¹ bounds the step's relative forward error:

    f = p(n)·eps·(1 + ‖F‖₂²)·‖L⁻¹‖₂·κ₂(E)²   (+ 2‖B‖‖F‖·eps·κ₂(W)‖K‖·‖L⁻¹‖₂ for a float64 K, W = R + BᵀXB; or form K by ddGain)

L⁻¹(W) = Σ(Fᵀ)ᵏWFᵏ is a positive map, so by Russo–Dye ‖L⁻¹‖₂ = ‖P‖₂ with P = L⁻¹(I) (×√n for the Frobenius/1-norm of newtonStep). Two free, non-circular bounds:
- lower, P ⪰ I + FᵀF: f_lo = eps‖F‖²(1+‖F‖²)/√n ≥ 1 proves the step has no guaranteed digit (uses only ‖F‖);
- upper, Hewer identity X₁ = L⁻¹(Q_K) ⪰ λ_min(Q_K)·P with ‖X̂‖ from the pencil solve (not the Stein solve): f_hi = p(n)eps(1+‖F‖²)‖X̂‖₂/λ_min(Q_K) < 1 proves certification. With S: λ_min(Q_K) ≥ λ_min(Q − SR⁻¹Sᵀ), once per problem.
- A computed P (one solve on the cached Schur factors) is self-referential when true f ≥ 1, so f from P has LAPACK sep/rcond status: standard estimate, not a proof; kept because singular Q_K (Q = CᵀC) is common, checked by falsifier 4.

Probe from the frozen literals (pure Python; P summed to convergence):

| row | n | ‖F‖₂ | ρ(F) | κ(E) | ‖X‖₂ | ‖P‖₂ | f_lo | f (P) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| amd64 zrwbig 12378 | 4 | 4.1e6 | 0.52 | 1.0 | 2.7e14 | 1.3e14 | 1.6e10 | 2.4e11 |
| zrwreg 26697 | 6 | 7.8e5 | 0.58 | 16 | 1.5e15 | 6.4e13 | 1.7e7 | 4.3e9 |
| zrwbig 28511 | 6 | 3.2e5 | power it. 1.15, unreliable on non-normal F; P series converged in 45 terms so ρ < 1 | 56 | 3.9e15 | 7.0e14 | 4.8e5 | 8.0e9 |
| zrwreg 28010 (NFET2G a) | 2 | 4.8e5 | 0.53 | 1.8 | 1.2e12 | 2.7e11 | 4.1e6 | 6.9e6 |

f_lo ≫ 1 on every probed row: the step is drawn from a set containing 0 and 1e-7‖X‖ alike, dips are luck, and the oracle-correct rows share the same f. Benign rows (‖F‖ ~ 10) have f ~ 1e-12. f_lo ≥ 1 ⇔ ‖F‖ ≳ 1e4, from eps, not tuned. Not probed: 17961 and the 2ARMRV rattle rows (no literals in hand); compute f before assuming the class.

Kantorovich/sep a-posteriori bounds are this same normwise quantity: cheap and rigorous, vacuous here by ~1e18. dd residual + float64 solve (refineDescriptorDare) sits at the same floor: residual-noise term eps²(1+‖F‖²)‖P‖₂ = 5e-7..3e-5, matching "106 bits stalled at 8e-9, 160 matched". So on these rows the only certificate is the extended Hewer fixed point: X within newtonTol of it, else take its iterate rounded, which fixes the named rows (CMKQI6 rescue). Derived precision p ≥ log2((1+‖F‖²)‖P‖₂) + 27 ≈ 118 bits on 12378; keep hewerGainPrecMin 128 as floor.

Per accept site (verifyRiccati :3665 it=0 for amd64 14201/27310; :3687 refine for the rest):
1. f_lo ≥ 1 → tier 2, no solve.
2. f_hi < 1 → certify: (1+f_hi)·step + quad ≤ newtonTol, quad = (f/eps)·step²·‖B‖²‖X‖/λ_min(R) (Hewer quadratic term through ‖P‖); residual noise eps·f·step is absorbed.
3. else one cached-factor Stein solve for P (ws.lyap aData = T, vs = U; no Dgees) → f < 1 certify as 2, else tier 2.
4. Tier-2 breakdown → Accuracy 1 (honest: nil-wrong → unverified, 320-bit confirms).

Care: L⁻¹(W) = ∫e^{A_Kᵀt}We^{A_Kt}dt is positive too, ‖L⁻¹‖₂ = ‖P_c‖₂ from one cached-factor Lyapunov solve, ‖L‖ ≤ 2‖A_K‖, f_hi via X₁ ⪰ λ_min(Q_K)P_c; no useful f_lo.

## 2. Doc contract

Band stays newtonTol, not condition-scaled: "nil: X is within about 1e-8 of the stabilizing solution of the stored data: a Newton step within newtonTol whose Stein (Lyapunov) solve is shown to carry the step's digits (eps·‖L‖‖L⁻¹‖ < 1), else an extended-precision Hewer fixed point within newtonTol of X. How far eps perturbations of the data move X is not reported." Data resolution is the census's job (sx), not the API's.

## 3. Cost within CEFUJP

- Measure first, no solver change: the census jsonl carries neither K nor ‖F‖, so the harness must emit ‖F‖₂, f_lo, f_hi per row on base; count f_lo ≥ 1 and f_hi ≥ 1 per set. Budget ≈ 0.5% − timing noise (~0.1%): z5a 72k → 122 is 0.17%; zrw 40k → 9 is 0.02%; zw46 12k → 15 is 0.13%; rv48 10k already 0.458% (27 of 34 are rows now running Hewer for K).
- Tier 1 is uniform: free when f_hi < 1; one cached-factor solve otherwise. Well under 2× per row at n ≤ 6 (ddMulAcc loops, not Dgees, dominate a step): measure.
- Tier 2 shares the extended run: one `extendedDare.model` per row certifies X, K and xe together, so rows already taking hewerGain* for K (rv48/rv49 reduced inputs, 28010) add nothing; only rows new to the extended path count against 0.5%.
- Breach lever order: P-solve f, then measured dd Stein residual of Δ̂ (‖P‖₂‖r₂‖ for p(n)eps‖F‖²‖Δ̂‖), never a constant. Still breaching → pay or demote, not waive.
- Care tier 2 does not exist (extendedDare/hewer, Smith doubling, discrete only). Rule Dare now; file "extended Newton–Kleinman, big-float Lyapunov" before any Care gate, else z5a's 122 become WORSE.
- BBN22I: a certified δX gives δK ≤ ‖W⁻¹‖‖B‖‖A‖δX, a derived K resolution to replace gainFloor/gainCap later; out of scope.

## 4. Falsifiers

1. A named or rattle row with f_lo < 1 and P-solve f < 1 from its literals: the noise is elsewhere (gain/W rounding); redo.
2. Extended Hewer at the derived precision disagrees with the 320-bit X by > newtonTol, or fails on an oracle-correct triggered row: precision or model wrong; raise p per the formula first.
3. Any oracle-correct Acc-0 row demoted after the change (expect 0: tier 2 certifies or corrects).
4. Any row certified by tier 1 with X beyond the census band: bound unsound (p(n), κ(E), K term, quad, or the P estimate); must be 0.
5. Any set > 0.5% rows > 2× once the trigger fires: population too large; escalate the lever order.
6. Many f ≥ 1 rows whose float64 step tracks the oracle error within 2×: loose for cost only; motivates the r₂ estimator.

title: CORE: Bandwidth +Inf with nil for continuous crossings below 1e-300 (endCrossings scan floor; ref RLCKVA)
body:
Found by the RLCKVA fixer (2026-11-12). Critical: wrong result with nil.
- **Bug:** Bandwidth returns +Inf with a nil error when a continuous crossing lies below about 1e-300. The endCrossings scan stops at tn < 1e-300 (margin.go:1341) without a sign change.
- **Repro:** A=[-p*1e8, p, 0, -p], B=[1.67, -0.38], C=[0.59e-300, -0.94e-300], D=1.04, dt=0, for p = 1e-302, 1e-305, 1e-307 and 3e-308. DCGain certifies (nil error). The oracle bandwidths are 9.984e-303, 9.976e-306, 9.976e-308 and 2.993e-308; Bandwidth returns +Inf with nil for all four.
- **Tried:** lowering the floor to 0x1p-1022 fixes 1e-302 and 1e-305 but not 1e-307 or 3e-308.
- **Direction:** under the Go error rule, return a correct value or an honest error (ErrAccuracyUnverified) when the scan reaches the floor without bracketing.
- **Repro files:** /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-josephj-workspace-controlsys/90f6527f-00fa-4f22-8ebb-64f8a65942a3/scratchpad/rlckva/zz_rl_floor_test.go, which needs zz_rl_probe_test.go and the rlckva harness.

- **Cross-ref:** RLCKVA.

RULING (coordinator, 2026-11-12): APPROVED as next in the non-Riccati slot after RLCKVA; no Fable needed. Below the scan floor, return a correct value (extend the scan in log-space, or solve the crossing on scaled data) or ErrAccuracyUnverified; never +Inf with nil. Use derived scaling (exact pow2), not a new floor. Census against the scale-aware oracle.

Fixer (2026-11-12): done at 1591320, stacked on RLCKVA 8748154; census at scratchpad/cwmcxc/run.sh (not run). Notes:
- Float64-range guards 2^1000 and 2^-1022 are not search floors; the coordinator is asked to confirm.

- 2^1000 (overflow guard) and 2^−1022 (subnormal limit) CONFIRMED as float64 representability limits, not search floors, provided hitting either returns ErrAccuracyUnverified and never nil. Say so in a code comment.

title: Riccati boundaryCertified gate band misses exact-unreachable boundary rows just outside n*eps*||A||_F
body:
Follow-up of DBOVA4 (wave 54). Several S-free, structurally exact rows stay Accuracy 0 and certified-wrong on base and branch, with 320-bit closed-loop margin 0..2.2e-16: zz54b seeds 1104 (Dare/Kalman, E), 1393 (Care/Kalman, E), 1973 (Care/Kalman) and 2052 (Dare/Kalman).
boundaryDeficient(detect) is true both unscaled and scaled, but the float Eig closest to the boundary sits 1.01-2.2x outside the gate band: 3.66e-15 vs 3.46e-15, 3.69e-15 vs 1.71e-15, 3.44e-15 vs 2.81e-15, 2.44e-15 vs 2.41e-15. So the cost test never runs.

body:

Sites (lqg.go):
- `currentGains`: `Sinv.Inverse(S)` on S = C·P·Cᵀ + Rn returns "Lqg: innovation covariance: ErrSingularEquation" on any error, including gonum's `mat.Condition` warning (the inverse is still computed).
- `floatNoiseGain`: `kw.Solve(G, …)` returns "Lqg: ErrSingularR" on the same warning.

Evidence (JGGEN2 census, rv46 gens, amd64 only; native fine):
- edge 92, edge 697: base Kalman returned a wrong gain at Acc1 (K 0.32 / 0.039 off the 320-bit reference), which kept S better conditioned. With JGGEN2's exact Kalman (Acc0), Lqg Current errors with "innovation covariance singular".
- bnd 227: LqgCur ok1 on base → "R matrix is singular" on cand.
- edge 361: errors on base and cand alike.

Expected: MATLAB lqg returns the controller. Decide by the actual conditioning: accept a `mat.Condition` warning when the result is finite and the residual is small, or certify by a bound. Error only on true singularity. Needs census scope from the coordinator (it changes value/error on finite data).

title: PERF: HinfSyn_D11/mimo +20% on gonum 30740af
body:
BenchmarkHinfSyn_D11/mimo 569us -> 683us (+20%, reproduced at n=12), allocs unchanged, on controlsys 6ff46d8 with gonum v0.20.10 -> 30740af. siso -6.7%. Geomean -0.22%. Done: cause identified with pprof evidence; fixed in gonum if fixable without losing reference parity, else documented as the parity cost.

Profile result (2026-11-04): cause gonum #39 7d43fc26 (Dtrsm Left divide). Bisect mimo/siso us: 374c0438 571/220; 7d43fc26 688/210; #40, #41 flat; 30740af with #39 reverted 600/225; 30740af with Left as a 1/a loop (old bits, divide-shaped loop) 601. The bits matter, not the divide cost: Dtrsm about 1% cumulative both sides, 156 calls/op, small (4x4, 6x6). Mechanism: ulp changes shift the climbed peak by 2e-11 (Gamma 0.51098515931400124 -> 0.51098515932509014), near certifyPeak's gammaLow*(1+tol/2) probe margin (norms.go), so mimo needs one more certify round: hasImagEigs 1->2, sigma 104->147, climb 1->2. siso flips the other way (137->107 sigma). Not fixable in gonum without losing reference parity; no kernel regressed. Proposed: close as path noise, or file controlsys EDGE on certifyPeak/climb convergence sensitivity if the mimo number matters. Note: #39 commit message wrongly says Right keeps the reciprocal; code divides in all four branches, matching dtrsm.f. Correct this in the release notes. Scratch: scratchpad/hinf.

Replay at 1200 bits with decisions frozen: 0:6358 raw last RQ 1x1 thr 1.58e-7, float 5.97e-5, exact 8.77e-5, 1ulp change 3.07e-4; pre 7.6e-9, 1.14e-6, 3.56e-6, 2.02e-5. 0:1302 raw thr 5.92e-12, float 5.63e-9, exact 4.45e-9, 1ulp 2.1e-8. So blocks are the data sensitivity, not rounding. Norm is not the fault; a small sigma kept fixes a rotation with angle error eta/sigma applied to larger neighbours (fits replay). Wedin level eta_next=max(eta,eta*||W||/sigma_kept), 384 rows, arm64/amd64: eta good->bad 148/149, bad->good 22/26; glob 159/160, 23/26; ideal (floored at measured 1ulp sensitivity, not implementable) 94/92, 25/25, breaking true controls 0:6990,1091,234,5114,5649. 41/168 class A and 221/314 class B reductions keep blocks under 10x sensitivity. No threshold can separate. Options: close or re-scope; route change compressing square rank-deficient models to normal rank k before the staircase (unmeasured, needs reliable k, touches 7MP62G). Out of scope: amd64 vs arm64 base differ on 9/384 identical input bits; H rows move with any rank change (T7WMMQ). Files: worker scratchpad gvd7as.

FABLE RULING (coordinator-adopted, 2026-11-12). Shared mechanism: leave the float rank decisions alone and certify the reduced object a-posteriori against the stored model, in two tiers. Tier 1: the response-interpolation certificate (frequencyAxisCutInBand, minimal_frequency_axis.go:64-241); for descriptors it needs a pencil generalisation of sensWork.bound with |s||E|+|A|. Tier 2: exact rational on the dyadic stored data for small n: reuse integerPencil + exactDetPoly (riccati_boundary_exact.go:187-258) with exactWithinBudget-style gates; don't copy ratDet. Fallback: value + ErrAccuracyUnverified, never a wrong nil.
GVD7AS: exact tier for square staircase rows (m=p, D singular) within budget, behind a sensitivity trigger. Exact normal rank k = max_j rank_exact(P(s_j)) over N=n+m+1 points. Exact regular-part det polynomial: exact-rational elimination for k<m. Determined vs infinite roots via the componentwise β(z) ≥ |z| (eigenRoundingBounds convention, no constant). Certify each returned zero by its Kantorovich disk inside β plus an equal count. When in budget, prefer the exact-derived answer (fixes rows rather than downgrading them). Trigger (perf only, never a decision): kept σ ≤ propagated first-order Wedin disk η. Out-of-budget and wide/tall rows: status quo, recorded as a contract gap. Falsifiers to measure first: trigger fire rate on broad CEFUJP sets >0.5% of unchanged rows; any exact vs 320-bit disagreement; trigger missing 0:1302, 0:6358, 0:5404. Order: after RLCKVA.

body:
Found in wave 11 (branch fix/wave11).

SLOWDOWN, large but tail-only: on the crowded-integrator sweep (den = s^m * tiny real roots 1e-10..1e-5, sometimes a tiny complex pair, plus one 1e-3..1 pole; 2000 cases, seed PCG(77,fam)), wall clock went from 42s on base to 1728s on the branch (41x). Worst cases: c1/0061 (num=[0.009773188260746423 0.04489604727967583 0.020323824184367914 0.025820219062960566 0.025797214642228176 0.006646947890672527 0.0211410669887515], den=[1 0.003649069685529213 2.4765632608475385e-08 1.738276564214012e-13 1.3318081161564088e-18 -1.5346094421104906e-24 0 0], tau=0.106793461122868, verdict U, matching the oracle) goes from 0.7ms to 26.9s. c1/0038 goes from 32ms to 34s and errors on both base and branch. c0/0474 (num=[6.147829022841792 10.216695150719099 7.832026243562451 3.0229141413956437 0.6108677798926465 0.060153027952126306 0.002148638203899052], den=[1 -0.46362065820370524 -8.844990464639967e-06 -5.1310852993591357e-11 -8.387818654264996e-17 0 0 0], tau=0.0034389605674428696): IsStable goes from 0.30s to 23.3s and DiskMargin from 0.68s to 22.9s.

Slowdown attribution: with 9e0e49a's margin_ddeval.go placed on base's delay_nyquist.go, c0/0474 still takes 21.6s. So the cause is the DOIFRS pivot test alone, not the formCluster order change or axisAt. The cost per solve is small (BenchmarkDDSISOSolve response 2661 to 2999 ns, noise 2594 to 2811 ns, about 1.1x). The cost is in how many solves run: the dd solve now succeeds where base failed early, so refine walks through the crowded band. The profile shows about 28% of the time in poleSpacing, which calls descriptorPolicy.poles and then Dgeev again on every evalWithPoleLimit call, and about 25% in ddSISOSolve. These two are the places to cut cost. The shipped tests are only mildly affected (TestDelayNyquistClusterSweep 85s to 96s).

Descriptor certifier reach collapses in the band between a crowded origin cluster and the next real pole. Repro: at 9e0e49a, set formCluster back to ascending k for dd, then run TestDelayNyquistTinyRealPolesDDCircles case 1 (den 1, 0.006386411776610228, 3.0129825054035514e-08, 1.2921688426134479e-17, 0, 0, 0; tau 0.025221635624798323). The dd pass verifies a k=4 cluster at g≈1.09e-7; the walk then returns refineBudget (2,097,152 points) at ω≈4.7107e-6 after about 15 s. Certified spans in [1e-7, 4.7e-6] average about 2e-12 wide. Files: delay_nyquist.go (refine, certifiedSpan), delay_nyquist_cert.go (descriptorCertifier kind 0/1 models). Descending k in the dd pass avoids it, but any walk that starts inside that band will hit the same budget wall.

title: CORE: Dare non-rLost red-nil pencil K returned without resolution check (dareInputs; bound-only; ref BBN22I)
body:
Found by the BBN22I fixer (2026-11-13). Possible wrong result with nil (Acc0), from a bound argument only; no repro yet.
- **Site:** dareInputs (riccati.go :1169 at 3aed79d). Non-rLost rows with red nil return the pencil K with no resolution check.
- **Bound argument:** with rLost false, κ·eps ≤ 1e-9·‖A−BK‖/(‖B‖₁‖K‖√m). So K can be unresolved only when ‖K‖ is more than 1e3× smaller than ‖A−BK‖/‖B‖.
- **Direction:** apply the same reject-only gainResolved check (W(K̂−K*) = BᵀδX(A−BK̂), δX = eps|X|) at that exit too, falling back to Hewer, else Accuracy 1.
- **Cross-ref:** BBN22I, BN4LWB.

body: From NGG5TW ruling2 (scratchpad ngg5tw/ruling2.md). Rule 8 is Rule 6 plus a δ-route bound |Cδ| as min, plus the a-priori term on the verify side. title: DECISION (decided, live): uncertified results are typed errors with optional partial result, not Accuracy flags; non-convergence is not ErrNoStabilizing
body:
User direction (2026-11-07): uncertified results must be explicit errors, not err==nil plus an Accuracy flag. Callers read err==nil as success; a second Accuracy check defeats the usual pattern.

Contract:
- Verified solution -> result, nil.
- Convergence or accuracy check failed -> optional partial result plus typed error (new sentinels, e.g. ErrNotConverged, ErrAccuracyUnverified). Partial result + error is valid Go; caller opts in via errors.Is.
- Conditioning estimates (Rcnd, KSens, etc.) stay as diagnostics on successful results.
- Non-convergence must NOT be reported as ErrNoStabilizing ("no stabilizing solution exists" is a mathematical claim). ErrNoStabilizing only when proved (e.g. unstabilizable boundary mode, Hamiltonian eigenvalues on the axis to within certified tolerance).

Scope (Accuracy int today): RiccatiResult (riccati.go:182; Care/Dare/Lqr/Lqe/Kalman/observer.go), H2SynResult, LqgResult, PolesResult (PolesDetail), LeastSquaresFit (C2DFit); ErrNoStabilizing returns in riccati.go (40 sites), riccati_extended.go, h2syn.go, hinfsyn.go. 8 non-test files read .Accuracy; ~50 test files.

Design questions for the DESIGN task: sentinel set and wrapping (one ErrAccuracyUnverified vs per-domain); whether a typed error carries the partial result (e.g. *UncertifiedError{Result}) or the function returns (res, err) with res non-nil; whether Accuracy field is removed or kept only as diagnostic; PolesDetail count-uncertified case; which current ErrNoStabilizing sites are really non-convergence.

Census rule impact: Accuracy 1 -> error with the same partial value is NOT value->error under the clean bar (value still returned, err now honest). Census must compare the partial value against the oracle band.
Interacts with 2BQZJY (Hewer in-band certificate): demotions Acc0->1 now surface as errors, so that task gains priority.
API break is OK (v2). File process-lab adaptation task.
Decided, live: governs ZOJBZX and all new result contracts. Kept open like ILI7DZ.
Scope boundary (2026-11-08, ZOJBZX Q8): the contract binds APIs that claim a certificate (Care/Dare family, H2Syn, Lqg, PolesDetail, C2DFit/C2D LS). Poles/Zeros and other MATLAB-tolerance decisions make no claim and stay MATLAB parity with nil error. User may overrule.
