title: PERF: EvalFr balancedDense/hessenbergSweep normwise pivot tol sends graded models to dd fallback
body:
Found in wave 17 (fix/wave17). Correct values, slow path (O(n^3) double-double per point). Componentwise pivot test on failure branch.

[w17 #68 edges] PERF (not wrong values): balancedDense.evalInto and hessenbergSweep.factor still use the normwise pivot tolerance n*scale*eps. Graded but finite realizations (e.g. a companion form of a wide-range polynomial TF) are therefore flagged singular at every point. They now get the correct value via the double-double fallback, which is O(n^3) double-double per point plus a pole search (poleSpacing). A componentwise pivot test on the failure branch only (track the row magnitudes the pivot was formed from; singular iff pivot <= n*eps*mag), with Hessenberg failures retried on a lazily built balancedDense, would keep such sweeps on the fast path. Files: frequency_hessenberg.go.

title: DESIGN: ZPKModel certification (per-route certificates, candidates, evaluator, weak/strong contract)
body:
DESIGN. Found by X5OSBB. ZPKModel never checks its final per-row ZPK against the stored model. Census on main 98dfbc7 (320-bit oracle, C-style windows; $S/x5osbb: zc-b3-*.tsv, cmp2-h4.txt, cmp2-h5.txt, zc.sh/zt.sh, zz_zpkcensus_test.go, zz_zpktiming_test.go): ~6,100 nil-wrong rows/arch (every nse-rot, planted, rotfast row; ~93% matched; ~70% matched-hid; ~10% fz), many stiff/near-singular-E explicit models with poles to ~1e15.

X5OSBB fixes only the uncertified TF.ZPK fallback route. A gate on every output (zpk_verify.go in X5OSBB WIP 6103f91: bounded model response vs ZPK evaluated with a derived γ_{4nz+7np} bound at axis probes + probes beside ZPK poles/zeros, n+deg+1 verified points, tol √ε) resolves ~6,000/arch but fails CEFUJP (fz 43%/35% >2× outcome-unchanged), leaves 147/131 nil-wrong (interpolation gaps, often s=0), and makes 490/492 matched-hid *-unc-* weak-only rows unverified (float Ĝ is rounding noise).

Scope:
- Per-route certificates: backward-error bounds for pencil eig and tzero.
- Better candidates before erroring (unreduced pencil, eig).
- Sharper evaluator for rows whose response is not boundable in float.
- OWNER DECISION: weak (within terms, like Reduce (C)) vs strong (pole/zero location) certification for ZPK — contract gap: doc promises only "fit the response at least as well as" the TF roots.
- Perf: per-probe bounded-response cost (related N7HDNC 1.92×).
Done when: contract decided; census on both arches 0 WORSE, nil-wrong ≤ documented residual; CEFUJP bar. Cross-ref X5OSBB, N7HDNC, NGG5TW.
First step: bring the weak/strong ZPK contract question with X5OSBB's 489-row evidence to the coordinator (Fable).

## RULING (coordinator-relayed; user decisions 2026-11-13, Fable advice adopted)
USER DECISIONS:
1. ZPKModel nil contract = "within terms", the same form as Reduce (C): |G_ij(s)−Z_ij(s)| ≤ tol·max(max_j|G_ij|, max_j|Z_ij|, Σ_l|C_il||X_lj(s)|+|D_ij|), with tol=√ε, at axis points outside the shared-pole windows. No per-root location accuracy is certified. Doc text: Fable's draft (advice file below), replacing "when they fit the response at least as well as…".
2. A row whose response lies below its terms at every axis point is certified nil by any Z within those terms, consistent with TransferFunction's rank floor. The 489 rows/arch are therefore base-correct; the WIP's unv on them is WORSE.
DESIGN (adopted):
- Symmetric check: verify when diff + ver_G + δ_Z ≤ tol·max(scale, terms − δterms); refute against terms + δterms. δterms from the componentwise |L̂||Û| bound. The WIP's asymmetry is the bug.
- One verifier for every route, run per row against the Sminreal'd row, with n_r+d_i+1 points counted per side of a spectral gap. Points: beside each Z root and each eigenvalue (values only); the static point, plus z=−1 for discrete; a geometric fill. No dense grids, no up-front eigenvectors, sharpening only at open points. Remove the pencil route's 1e-12/1e-9 misfit gate.
- Candidates in order: (a) reduced pencil; (b) unreduced pencil with closest pole/zero pairs cancelled under a certified cancellation; (c) eig + TF zeros; (d) TF roots. On failure: MATLAB-style eig+tzero with ErrAccuracyUnverified. This departs from the X5OSBB narrowed ruling (which kept TF roots); departure ACCEPTED, record it.
- Descriptor "na" rows (2,512 fz, all base-correct) stay nil without a certificate, as a DOCUMENTED departure. Follow-up CORE task filed: bounded sE−A solve for ZPKModel descriptor rows.
FALSIFIERS (measure first; any hit → stop and report):
- F0: any gate-verified row with oracle weak >1 (must be 0).
- F1: on the 489 rows, print terms and δterms at the trace points; confirm δterms < terms with |Ĝ|+ver ≤ tol·terms.
- F2: fz fb ok→ok / pc ok→ok rows over 2×. More than 100 → Stage B (Schur-based bounded evaluator).
- F3: residual still worst at s=0 after per-side counting.
- F4: pencil-route nil-wrong ≠ 0.
- F5: any base-ok row → unv.
Bar: 0 WORSE, nil-wrong ≤ documented residual, CEFUJP met. Resume from wip/X5OSBB; one task with JW5H7V.
PRIORITY: largest critical item (~6,100 rows/arch). Non-Riccati order: 5Z5U2F → VFM6MN → JW5H7V+X5OSBB → RLCKVA → GVD7AS → 5CNIZA.

### Fable advice (verbatim, jw5h7v-advice.md)
# JW5H7V advice (draft)

DECISION: contract W = Reduce (C) "within terms", applied symmetrically (verify AND refute against tol·max(scale, terms)); no root-location accuracy certified. One certificate for every route (pencil route loses its 1e-12/1e-9 gate): a minimal structured probe set against the row's exact structurally minimal part. Candidates ordered pencil(reduced) > pencil(unreduced, cancelled pairs) > eig+TF zeros > TF roots; on failure return MATLAB's eig+tzero with ErrAccuracyUnverified.

## 1. Contract

Three readings, base census (zc-b3, routes from h6, per arch):
- W (Reduce (C)): |G−Z| ≤ tol·max(scale, Σ|C||X|+|D|). The 489: weak 5e-4–2.5e-3 → base-correct; WIP unv = WORSE, a gate deficiency.
- R (response/scale only): the 489 are 6.7e7·tol off → honest unv. But ~820 rows/arch are weak-only (fz/pc 116, matched/pc 103, matched-hid/pc 72, matched-hid/fb 495, fz/fb 35); 290 of them are pencil-route rows with eig/tzero roots, and the h4 gate verified every one except the 489 at tol·scale at n+deg+1 points: under R they become gate-verified nil-wrong residuals. R's extra demand is neither certifiable nor refutable in float64 near a transmission zero (a k-fold zero at z=−1 moves by ε^{1/k}). Not a contract.
- L (locations in derived disks): coefficient-close ≠ root-close; clusters ZPKModel exists for get disks ~ε^{1/k}‖A‖ (β≈0.1 on the 489's 7-cluster); L⇒response needs Σ r_k/|Re p̂_k| ≤ tol, fails near the axis; costs eigenvectors (~3× eig) plus a location oracle in the census. Reject as the nil contract; optional v2 add-on (ZPKResult.PoleBounds).

Probe (h6 binary, TestX5Rows+trace, matched-hid/0-unc-true): n=8, TF row degree 1, ZPK = one pole 0.998, gain 1.6e-16, i.e. Z≈0; Ĝ is noise at all 19 probes (comp≈|Ĝ|, ver≈100|Ĝ|); β≈0.1 on the 7-cluster at z≈1. The response of this realization is not computable in float64 anywhere on the axis; TransferFunction's rank floor already resolved it at the terms scale. Under W the TF's answer is correct and any Z below tol·terms certifies: that is the documented limit of (C), inherited from TF. Not a hidden-mode/terms inflation: the mode is rotated, Sminreal will not change it.

Symmetric verification is rigorous: diff + ver_G + δ_Z ≤ tol·max(scale, terms_G+|D|) ⇒ |Z−G| ≤ that. The 489 pass iff |Ĝ|+ver ≤ tol·terms (growth ≲1e5): falsifier F1.

Doc text (replaces "when they fit the response at least as well as ..."):
"A nil error certifies, for every output row i of an explicit delay-free model, within the limits of the sampled check (zpkVerifiedRow), at every axis point s outside the windows of the poles the row shares with the model (zpkSharedPoleWindows),
	|G_ij(s) − Z_ij(s)| ≤ tol·max(max_j |G_ij(s)|, max_j |Z_ij(s)|, Σ_l |C_il||X_lj(s)| + |D_ij|), tol = √ε,
G and X = (sI−A)⁻¹B exact for the stored data and Z the returned roots and gains evaluated exactly. The terms exceed |G_ij| only where the response cancels, as at a transmission zero, below which no roots computed in floating point place the zero; a row whose response lies below its terms at every axis point is not determined by its data in floating point, and any Z within tol of those terms certifies it, as TransferFunction's rank floor already resolves it. The check uses points beside every pole and zero of Z and every eigenvalue of the row's structurally minimal part, the static point, and a geometric fill, with n_r + d_i + 1 verified points (n_r the order of that part, d_i the row degree), on each side of a spectral gap; agreement there fixes a rational difference of that degree in exact arithmetic but does not bound it between the points. No location accuracy of individual roots is certified: a k-fold root is determined only to ε^{1/k} and a pole in a shared window only to its rounding bound. A row no candidate verifies is returned with its pencil roots (poles eig(A), zeros of the system pencil, as MATLAB zpk(ss)) and an error wrapping ErrAccuracyUnverified."

## 2. Certificate (CEFUJP by construction)

- One verifier for all routes, per row, against ref (Sminreal'd row: exact restriction, order n_r ≤ n; count n_r+d_i+1, not n+d_i+1; SISO rows identical cost).
- Points: beside each ZPK root (eigenAxisProbes on Z's roots), beside each eigenvalue of ref (values only; the pencil route already has them), static point, z=−1 for discrete, geometric fill to the count. No gapProbePoints/decadeAxisProbes grids.
- No eigenvectors up front: β/ρ windows computed lazily, only when a root-adjacent point is open; sharpen only open points; pooled buffers. The WIP's 2× came from EigenBoth + 20–80 points + sharpening on the full sys.
- Per-side count across a spectral gap (Reduce's rule): fixes the s=0 class of the 147/131 residual (106/97 fz rows whose worst point is a probe at s=0 that was open while the fast side filled the count).
- Exact axis poles (β_j = 0, structurally zero row/column): Z must carry them exactly, a structural check; near-axis: window rule.
- Refutation (diff − comp > tol·max(scale, terms), outside windows) only drops a candidate.
- Stage B, only if zt shows >0.5% of unchanged-outcome rows >2×: Schur-based bounded evaluator, O(n_r²)/point (T = QᵀAQ, a-posteriori η = ‖A − QTQᵀ‖, triangular-solve bounds).
- Not: per-root a-posteriori location certificates as the certificate (see L). Markov bound |c||A|^{r−1}|b|·γ stays as a candidate filter.
- Descriptor rows ("na": 2512 fz, all base-correct): nil today without a certificate. Follow-up task: bounded descriptor solve on sE−A chained through TF's explicit reduction. Do not unv them (2512 WORSE).

## 3. Candidates (first verified wins; refuted dropped)

(a) reduced pencil (current): eig(A_red), tzero per channel, Markov gain.
(b) unreduced pencil when Reduce declines or n_r > d_i: eig(A_ref), tzero(ref), cancel the n_r−d_i closest pole/zero pairs ordered by |p̂−ẑ|/max(dist(p̂,axis), ρ); a pair with |p̂−ẑ| ≤ tol·dist(p̂,axis) is a certified-dropped factor (|(s−ẑ)/(s−p̂) − 1| ≤ |p̂−ẑ|/|s−p̂|).
(c) eig(A_ref) poles + TF numerator zeros, static-fit gain (tzero count off).
(d) TF roots (current fallback).
Failure: return the first order-consistent candidate with ErrAccuracyUnverified; (a)/(b) are MATLAB zpk(ss) (doc: "zero and pole"); TF roots are O(1) off on clusters (HP3RZO). Departs from the X5OSBB narrowed ruling (kept TF roots): flag.
The pencil route's 2,437/2,487 nil-wrong rows/arch go through the same certificate.

## 4. Falsifiers

F1 489 rows do not verify within terms with plain ver → sharpen (comp); then dd; if comp fails → owner call (honest unv but WORSE).
F2 zt on fz fb:ok→ok (2264) and pc:ok→ok (9639): >100 rows >2× → Stage B.
F3 residual after per-side counting still has worst probe at s=0 → gap is not interpolation; require the static point.
F4 pencil-route nil-wrong (matched/pc 891 …) not 0 after the certificate → window rule too wide (compare zcWindows vs zpkSharedPoleWindows).
F5 any R-ok base row → unv under candidate reordering = WORSE → ordering bug.
Owner flag: symmetric W makes vacuous certification explicit (489 rows: 1 pole for an 8-state model). A policy clause "response below terms everywhere → ErrAccuracyUnverified" would be a documented contract clause, not a tuned threshold, but is WORSE by the classifier as written.

- **Class A, 453 arm64 / 454 amd64 rows:** δterms ≥ terms near the z≈1 cluster (median |z−1| 0.008). δterms/terms has median about 5e3, max 4.7e6. The a-priori bound is valid (320-bit, orT_ap ≤ 1); terms are genuinely undetermined (|T̂−T|/T median about 1, up to about 500). The compensated bound is worse (up to 1.2e9).

## F1 RULING (Fable, coordinator-adopted, 2026-11-12), verbatim from jw5h7v-f1-ruling.md
# JW5H7V F1 ruling (final)

RULING: Option 2 — plain-float symmetric check against tol·max(scale, T̂ − δ_ap), structured points plus fill doubled per round (≤3 rounds, stop when the verified count is met) — with dd only as a measured fallback. δ_ap only, never δ_cmp; no refinement-based sharpening anywhere in the gate; Reduce's gap rule kept verbatim, no finer distribution rule; a structured-point concession list closes the gap class.

New evidence (f1 pts/rows, both arches, read-only awk):
- δ_ap holds against the oracle at all 46,900 points. δ_post (|M̂⁻¹|R) is violated at 1–6 points/arch, every one with δ_ap ≥ T̂. δ_cmp (refined û) is violated at 22–26 points/arch, every one with δ_ap < T̂ — where the terms ARE determined. So plain inverse-based bounds are sound inside the gate δ_ap < T̂; the refinement step û += M̂⁻¹r̂ is unsound even inside it. Rule: T̂, δ_ap, ver, comp from the unrefined GEPP Û; if sharpening, sharpenAt(k, false) (compensated residual, no refinement). classifyProbe sharpens with refinement on the same path → Reduce risk is now evidence, not inference: file a task.
- ρ: rho0 = nε‖A‖ (normwise), rho[k] = min(rho0, 2nβ_k) needs β (EigenBoth). Lazy plan stands with a precise trigger: compute β only when a structured point lies within rho0 of an eigenvalue (then drop vs judge by rho[k]) or a window is needed; otherwise no eigenvectors. F2 cost estimate unchanged for ordinary rows.

(a) Soundness. At a point with δ_ap ≥ T̂ the only lower bound on the contract RHS is scale, so the check is the strong check: pass ⇒ rigorously verified (|Z−G| ≤ tol·max(|G|,|Z|)(1+O(tol))), counts; fail ⇒ uninformative — the oracle shows T̂ itself off by 1–500× there, nothing to recover — never counted, never refuting, never sharpened. Certifying from far-side verified points while the cluster-region response is undetermined is the sampled-check caveat plus decision (ii); doc wording: "verified where the data determine the terms". dd (δ/T ~3e-10) would verify cluster points but at 10–20× per point on 489 outcome-unchanged rows, 24% of matched-hid → CEFUJP fails; fallback only.

(b) Per-side. Reduce's rule is visibility: a point at |s| ≥ |λ|/tol cannot see λ to tol, hence the 1/√ε gap and two-sided counts. At 1.3 decades it is vacuous; keep it verbatim for the stiff sets (planted/rotfast/nse-rot have real 1e8 gaps). A finer cumulative rule (#verified{|s| ≤ σ_k} ≥ #roots{σ ≤ σ_k}+1) is derivable but needs cluster-region verified points, which the 489 cannot supply → unv → contradicts (ii). Replacement: structured points — beside each Z root, each ref eigenvalue, the static point, z=−1 — each verified or conceded. Concessions: inside a shared-pole window; dropped within nε|s|+ρ_k (the census's ρ, so β when within rho0); δ_ap ≥ T̂. Open with determined terms → compensated (no refinement) → still open → unv. Count n_r+d+1 from verified points anywhere; fill rounds as WIP; ~21 points on lean rows, ~63 on the 489.

(c) 87/89 and s=0. Diagnosis OPEN: the probe ran matched-hid keys only (f1Sys), so "gap, not false certification" is not established for them. Two mechanisms, both fixed by this ruling: a gap (worst structured point left open while far points filled the count) → structured-point rule; a false point verification through refined sharpening (now evidenced on the 489's points) → no-refinement rule plus the δ_ap gate on ver/comp. Discriminator for the coordinator's run (extend f1Sys to fz/matched keys): at the oracle's worst point, did the WIP gate mark that point verified (false cert → bound bug) or open (gap)? Residual after the fix: rows whose worst point is conceded by δ_ap ≥ T̂ — a sampled-check residual the census counts as nil-wrong (documented residual, not a (ii) concession). F3′ counts it; no threshold patch.

(d) dd and CEFUJP. Trigger only on rows still open after the fill rounds, only at open structured points (≤ 2(n_r+d)+2 dd solves). Otherwise-unv rows are exempt; rows dd rescues count. Ship without dd; census: open-after-fill ∧ base nil-correct — expected 0 (WIP set 489/489; class B passes the symmetric check). Nonzero and <0.5%/set → second PR; above → owner decides WORSE vs perf bar.

F5 closure: lean set + iterated fill must give 489/489 and 0 base-ok→unv on both arches before PR.

  - 6/4 fz rows with weak 1.09–4.06 are unsampled gaps: 3/1 sit beside another row's Z root, 3/3 sit on census-grid-only points.
- **Interpretations awaiting confirmation:**
  - GEPP zero pivot is treated as δ_ap=∞ (conceded). TestZPKModelRotatedDoubleIntegratorKeepsMarkovGain stays nil with Z(0) about 3e7·√ε off.
  - On failure, return the first candidate formed rather than raw eig+tzero, which is not RowDegrees-consistent.
  - Degree-0 rows stay unverified.
- **Unmeasured risk:** the verifier now runs on ~10,500 base-ok pencil rows. On stiff models plain ver is ~1e-4|Ĝ|.
- **Owner branches:** (1) a tighter complex LU constant (closes the 489, not unobs); (2) dd at open structured points (closes both); (3) accept the rows as a second PR, which conflicts with the F5 489/489 line; (4) loosen the structured-point rule, which reopens the s=0 gap.
- **Data:** scratchpad/jw5h7v/v1-*.tsv.

## v1 RULING (Fable, coordinator-adopted, 2026-11-12), verbatim from jw5h7v-v1-ruling.md. It CORRECTS the F1 ruling's attribution of the δ_cmp violations: the cause is the missing γ_{n+1}·T̂ formation term, not refinement.
# JW5H7V v1 ruling (final)

RULING: branch 2, staged. Stage 1: re-enable refinement under a derived convergence factor, add the missing formation term to every terms bound, derive the GEPP constant; measure. Stage 2: dd on rows that would otherwise be unverified, plus zero-pivot points on any row. Zero pivot is not a concession. Failure returns the first order-consistent candidate. No p× root sharing, no dense grids; census-grid gaps are the documented residual.

Correction to my F1 ruling (advisor-reconciled). The δ_cmp "violations" sit at δ_ap/T̂ ≈ 1e-13–1e-11 with |T̂−T|/T ≈ 1e-16–1e-15 and orT_cmp 1.0–1.8, and the probe computed cmp0 on the unrefined u0: refinement was not in the loop. It is the rounding of forming T̂ = Σ|Ĉ||Û| (γ_{n+1}·T̂ plus complex |·|), which δ_cmp omits and δ_ap's slack hides. Discriminator on f1 pts (both arches): refinement worsens the terms error (>2×) at 1796/1593 points, all with δ_ap/T̂ ≥ 1; at δ_ap/T̂ < 1 it improves 99.9% of 15,161/15,008 points (the 16/13 exceptions have both errors ≤ 1e-12, noise). Rule: η = γ·‖|W|‖_∞·‖|L_f||U_f|‖_∞ from termsBound's factors; refine only when η < 1; every bound using the computed inverse — comp, ver's a-priori term, δ_ap — carries 1/(1−η); every terms bound adds γ_{n+1}·T̂. Not optional: stiff rows (‖A‖~1e9, plain ver ~1e-4|Ĝ|) verify only through refinement (κε per pass), as Reduce does; without it planted/pc 134 and kalman-d0/pc 284 base-ok rows go unv.

(1) Branch and dd trigger. Stage 1 = η-gated refinement + formation term + the GEPP constant derived (Higham Thm 9.4 with the complex-product constant; derive, apply the factor, then see whether 83/389 and the unobs route-(a) rows close — do not predict). Stage 2 = complex-dd GEPP with the same a-priori formulas at u = 2⁻¹⁰⁴ (ddRealizationInto carries no bounds), triggered row-level: a row still open after the fill rounds gets dd at its open and undetermined structured and fill points; point-level: any structured point where double GEPP meets an exactly zero pivot. Rows that verified in double keep the undetermined concession (decision ii), so its residual exists only there. Cost: triggered rows are otherwise unv (exempt) unless rescued; rescued rows count toward the 0.5%/set clause — at most 83/389/496 plus the unobs remainder on matched-hid; stage 1 decides how many remain. Measure.

(2) Interpretations. Zero pivot: a failed computation, not a measurement that the terms are undetermined; conceding it is a contract hole — the DI test certifies Z(0) 3e7√ε off at a point the census judges and the headline claims. Rule: zero pivot → dd at that point; concede only if dd also pivots exactly zero (stored matrix exactly singular at s: an exact axis pole, which the census skips too). Expectation for the DI: dd resolves det(A), Ĝ(0) determined, Z(0) refuted, likely (d) too → unv; the re-freeze decides, with oracle numbers as for the other three tests. Failure return: first formed order-consistent candidate — agreed; RowDegrees is the contract and raw eig+tzero can break it. Degree-0 rows: n_r = 0 → Z = D = G exactly, nil; n_r > 0 (dynamics under TF's rank floor) → verify the candidate Z = D with n_r+1 points, unv if not. Headline: "at every axis point where the stored realization determines its terms in floating point (δ_ap < T̂), outside shared-pole windows"; the concession residual (F3′ 4/1 unobs rows) is counted and documented, not patched.

(3) Gaps. Do not add other rows' roots: a root of row k absent from eig(ref_i) is structurally decoupled from row i, which is smooth there; the census caught a generic gap. Census-grid-only gaps (3/3) are the sampled check's residual: no finite node set bounds a tolerance-verified rational difference uniformly on the axis, so a denser fill only moves them. 6/4 of ~14,000 base-ok fz rows (0.04%) → document; fill stays shortfall-sized.

(4) Before PR on the 10,500 pencil rows. (a) Stage 1 in, then census both arches: ok→unv on any base-ok pencil row = WORSE; watch planted/pc 134, kalman-d0/pc 284, matched/pc 48. (b) Point-level F0 on a stiff sample (f1-style harness extended to fz/planted/kalman keys), refinement ON: no verified point with oracle weak > 1. (c) zt both arches: ≤0.5%/set >2× among outcome-unchanged rows, fz/pc 9639 included. (d) Re-frozen tests plus DI with oracle numbers; FuzzSSToTF green. (e) Residual ledger by key, both arches: F3′ rows, census-grid gaps.

## REWORK RULINGS (coordinator, 2026-11-13)

### 1. ok→unv 12/9: HONEST, CONDITIONAL
- Confirm each dd-refuting point with the 320-bit oracle: |Z−G| > tol·max(scale, terms) at that s.

body:
From the JW5H7V F1 ruling (Fable, coordinator-adopted, 2026-11-12). Reduce classifyProbe sharpens with refinement (û+=M̂⁻¹r̂), which is unsound when κε>1. Evidence from the JW5H7V F1 probe (scratchpad/jw5h7v/):
- the δ_cmp bound is violated inside δ_ap<T̂, at 22–26 points per arch even where the terms are determined;
- the refined Û moves terms further from exact on about 250 rows per arch.

CORRECTION (JW5H7V v1 ruling, Fable, 2026-11-12): the δ_cmp violations were NOT caused by refinement. The probe computed cmp0 on the unrefined u0; the violations come from the missing rounding term for forming T̂=Σ|Ĉ||Û| (γ_{n+1}·T̂ plus the complex |·|). Refinement improves terms at 99.9% of points with δ_ap/T̂<1 and worsens them only where δ_ap/T̂≥1. New direction: gate refinement by η = γ·‖|W|‖_∞·‖|L_f||U_f|‖_∞ < 1, give every inverse-based bound 1/(1−η), and add γ_{n+1}·T̂ to every terms bound. Ruling: jw5h7v-v1-ruling.md (copy on JW5H7V).

title: LOW: finite-pole-count certificate redesign — needs advisor design ruling first (ELT76F parked; 2nd failed approach)
body:
Follow-up of ELT76F (wave 54, parked at origin parked/descriptor-elt76f-staircase 76a7a1e; findings F1-F3 and the decided-rate table are on ELT76F).
Problem: a per-level singular value at level >= 1 cannot tell a chain zero from a true pole under a tiny block determinant. Example: rvb cpx:2531, L3 1.9e-17 = 0.0425*tau_E, while the pole -3.01e8±2.23e8i has eigenvalue sensitivity S 6.1e9, so MATLAB eig(A,E) recovers it. Hi drops it, so the "never fewer than Hi" follow-on would lose real poles.
Candidates (need an advisor approach ruling before code; 5th attempt in this area):
(a) Make the 2^-100 / memo-band eigenvalue-sensitivity classifier the certificate (approach D).
(b) A pencil-aware deep-level zero rule, e.g. test the finite block's determinant/eigenvalue conditioning instead of sigma alone.
(c) Fix F3: theta_Q = max(tau_E, deflated sv)/gap.
Also rule the classifier threshold: S*u < 1 excludes 15/18 literals; the memo band (true S < 1e10, smear > 1e14) excludes 4/18.
Gate: Lo <= structural <= Hi on classifier-confirmed cases of rvb two/cpx/tri/bigA/edge plus chain/condChain; exclusion guard (662da74) enforced in committed tests; decided rate >= ~50% per generator or a stated reason.
Start from the parked branch's tests: certificate, oracle and literals. Generators: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-josephj-workspace-controlsys/90f6527f-00fa-4f22-8ebb-64f8a65942a3/scratchpad/w54review/elt/zz_elt2_rvbbuild_test.go and zz_elt2_rvb_sweep_test.go.
4ZWFL5 (arch-dependent deflateStiffChain) is sequenced after ELT76F and needs this oracle.
Files: new *_test.go only until the follow-on.

## Coordinator gate (wave 54)
This is the second failed approach on this problem. No code slot until an advisor design ruling is recorded here.
The ruling must explain how the design separates real stiff poles from chain residue at the same scale. F1 shows no absolute floor can.
It must include a dump-only feasibility step, like ELT76F Step 1, on the 18 literals and the rvb two/cpx sets.
If the advisor concludes a fully decided verifier is not achievable, there are two acceptable outcomes:
- a bracketing-only deliverable (Lo <= structural <= Hi, decided rate reported);
- close the task with the reason recorded.
Never a third fix round.
Priority: below the ready CORE work.
## Design proposal (wave 56, advisor-reviewed draft, for the coordinator ruling)
# L4BCTU design proposal: finite-pole-count certificate for descriptor (A, E), revision 2

Design only, for the coordinator's ruling. No library code, no commits, no ergo writes.

**Base and probe setup.** Base is origin/main 200863b. The probes ran in a detached worktree of 200863b, removed
afterwards. The worktree also carried:
- the four test files from origin/parked/descriptor-elt76f-staircase 76a7a1e (`descriptor_pole_count_*_test.go`);
- the generators reproduced in Appendix A.

"amd64" means GOARCH=amd64 under Rosetta, as in the project's local gate.

**Evidence tags.** [V] verified by a probe here; [T] taken from a task body or the parked branch (cited); [U] unverified.

This file does not depend on the scratchpad. Appendix A holds every generator, stream and seed. Appendix B gives the
durable locations of the literal matrices (ergo task bodies, origin branches, in-repo tests).

---

## 0. Plain consequence and decisions

**Under the recommended C2, the ELT76F/IP4PC3/L4BCTU repro rows are NOT fixed.** They become documented float64
resolution limits. Poles, IsProper and TF keep their current outputs on those rows: Poles keeps the base superset with
smear and may lack an F1 pole, TF/IsProper keep the current value or error. Nothing in production changes.

**Numbered decisions for the coordinator:**
1. **Which perturbation model defines "finite".** The MATLAB parity rule cannot decide F1 (section 4). Options:
   - (a) the normwise MATLAB-rank class. This matches RL6IT7 and LAPACK backward stability; F1 is then "ambiguous" and
     dropping it is acceptable.
   - (b) per-entry data resolution at δ = u. F1 poles are then real, but no float64 method measured here computes them.
2. **Retire "never fewer than Hi" for IP4PC3.** Hi (the exact staircase) is not an upper bound of the per-entry truth;
   F1 shows it.
3. **The 662da74 exclusion guard will trip under C2.** The saved ELT76F sweeps exclude about 25% of rvb two (F1
   171/1000 plus F2 ~93/1000) and about 5% of cpx (52/1000). Is an exclusion that *is* the finding a pass with a
   reason, or a fail?
4. **C1 as a production refute guard: not recommended.** (a) and (b) in section 3 show it never fires on a row whose
   staircase count or Poles count is correct (0 of 60 on arm64, 0 of 62 on amd64). But:
   - 38 of its 60 triggered rows have a TF that is already correct, so a TF/IsProper fail-closed consumer would turn

## 1. Problem class

### 1.1 Statement

Take a regular pencil (A, E) with singular E and an infinite Jordan chain of length k ≥ 2. Beside the chain sits a
finite block that is either small in E or large in A. The sizes involved:
- σ_s ≪ σ₁(E), but above MATLAB's rank floor τ_E = n·eps(σ₁(E)) (eigdecomp.go:1238-1243);
- or the finite pole is large because A is.

**How nf is decided today.** The finite count nf drives Poles and the finite/infinite split behind TF, IsProper and
dss2ss. It is set by one of three mechanisms:
- the level singular values of `deflateStaircase` (eigdecomp.go:517-663). Level 0 uses `descriptorRank` with full
  MATLAB rank. Levels ≥ 1 use `stiffChainRank(sv, 1e3·n·ε·σ₁, stiffPoles)` (:590, :773-786), with the 1e3 `ratio`
  at :554 and the stiff counter at :584-588;
- or the whole-pencil QZ |β|/|α| rules in `generalizedPoles` (descriptor.go:188-231);
- in the stiff-E, index ≥ 2 branch (:212-215), `tol = 0`, so only β = 0 counts as infinite.

**Failure directions:**
- **Short count.** A true pole's direction produces a deflated-level value that the level zeroes. Examples from the
  ELT76F step-1 ruling:
  - 5093 L4 7.5e-16;
  - 5552 L3 3.87e-14;
  - 12 L3 1.10e-14;
  - 357 L6 1.75e-13.

  All lie in (τ_E, 1e3·n·ε·σ₁]. The F1 case cpx 2531 L3 is 1.9e-17 = 0.0425·τ_E, below even the floor. [T]
- **Long count.** The QZ smear of a chain (|λ| ~ ε^(-1/k)) is kept by the tol = 0 branch. [T/V]

**Why no per-level floor decides F1.** A level-j singular value s is the norm of an exact perturbation of E, since
orthogonal transforms preserve norms. Zeroing s therefore yields a pencil within ‖ΔE‖ = s that has one more infinite
eigenvalue. For F1, s < τ_E, so both counts are inside the normwise MATLAB-rank class.

## 2. Why the prior approaches failed

1. **Float64 guards** (count by singular value; carriesAll/stablePencilEigs with a √ε cutoff; a jitter test with
   jitterResolvedTol 1e-2 on the deflated set; 1/λ matching). From ELT76F and IP4PC3: "smear members and true huge
   poles both have β ≠ 0".
   - Wave 41 dropped a true pole that moved more than √ε (F4OPPD blocker).
   - Wave 44 jitter-tested a set the staircase had already shortened: "jitter test passes because leftovers are smear".
   - The staircase's own rounding (the leak at eigdecomp.go:643, n·u·‖A‖/σa) exceeds the MATLAB floor, so the 1e3
     factor at :554/:590 acts as a G factor (step-1 ruling 1). [T]
2. **The exact big.Float staircase** (parked 76a7a1e). Three zones per level, E-side Davis-Kahan ρ, deliverable Hi
   (zero s ≤ τ_E):
   - **F1:** Hi drops a classifier-resolved stiff pole at level ≥ 1. Rates: cpx 52/1000 and two 171/1000
     band-confirmed; 45/700 and 117/700 fresh.
   - **F2:** every Decided result on rvb two contradicts the structural count; this is data-ambiguous.
   - **F3:** on the Lo path, θ_Q = τ_E/gap under-covers (edge 2232 1.8×, edge 13 3.1×).
   - **Classifier:** S·2^-53 < 1 excludes 15 of 18 literals; the memo band excludes 4 of 18.
   - **Decided rate** under 50% on every generator except condChain. [T]
3. **This pass:** F1 is a model mismatch. The F1 poles are resolved per entry at u (O4), while no normwise-stable
   float64 method sees them:
   - float QZ omits the pair (2531, 7001);
   - jitter moves them O(1) (two 11);
   - the float staircase drops them.

   Hi is a normwise statement, but its gate compared it with a per-entry/linearised oracle. [V]

### C1. Jitter-certified whole-pencil lower bound (refute-only)

**Algorithm.**
1. Whole-pencil QZ (already computed at descriptor.go:190).
2. Drop the eigenvalues that are `qzInfinite` at qzInfiniteTol(100·n·ε, ‖A‖₂, ‖E‖₂) (eigdecomp.go:1081/1088).
3. Recompute QZ on `leakDraws` (:744) jittered copies, using the `leakedZeros` recipe (:676-713).

5. L = the number certified.
6. A staircase count nf_stair is refuted iff nf_stair < L. U = r₀, the level-0 MATLAB rank (`descriptorRank` full,
   :1238).

Code is in Appendix A.3.

## 4. MATLAB counterpart

Fetched 2026-10-29.

- **pole** (https://www.mathworks.com/help/control/ref/dynamicsystem.pole.html): the poles are "the generalized
  eigenvalues of A – λE in the descriptor case." The page has no rule for dropping infinite ones. It warns: "Multiple
  poles are numerically sensitive and cannot be computed with high accuracy". A multiplicity-m pole gives a cluster of
  radius ~ε^(1/m), the same Puiseux smear seen at ∞ here.
- **isproper** (https://www.mathworks.com/help/control/ref/dynamicsystem.isproper.html): a descriptor with singular E
  is proper "if the model has at least as many poles as zeros." The page names no algorithm.
- **dss** (https://www.mathworks.com/help/control/ref/dss.html) and **tf**
  (https://www.mathworks.com/help/control/ref/tf.html): nothing on singular E, infinite modes or improper conversion.
- **tzero** (https://www.mathworks.com/help/control/ref/dynamicsystem.tzero.html): "based on SLICOT routines AB08ND,
  AB08NZ, AG08BD, and AG08BZ". A larger tolerance helps "eliminate very large zeros (near infinity)".
- dss2ss and the descriptor user-guide page returned 404.

**Finding.** The documented rule (finite generalized eigenvalues; isproper by counts) has no numerical definition of
"finite" in the smear band. Parity therefore cannot decide F1, so decision 1 must choose the perturbation model.

**UNVERIFIED GUESS, not evidence:** MATLAB's eig(A, E) is LAPACK QZ, and float64 QZ here omits the F1 poles, so MATLAB
might drop them too. MATLAB was not run.

  -candidate .` on the descriptor Poles/TF benchmarks: base-correct rows >2× slower ≤ 0.5% per set and arch.

---

## 7. Recommendation

**C2 (bracketing-only), with C1 as census metric and C3 optional.** Checks (a) and (b) did not change it.

**Why not "C2 + C1 refute-only":**
1. (a) confirms C1 fires only on rows with a wrong count, so a Poles-side cost would be Y6WWVQ-exempt. But 38 of 60 of
   those rows have a correct TF, so the only consumer where refute-only changes output (TF/IsProper fail-closed) breaks
   0 value→error.
2. In Poles, refute-only keeps base and so changes nothing until an accept path exists.
3. (b) shows C1 adds 32 arch flips that the staircase does not have.

**Why C2:**
- It is deterministic, already built, and passes on three arches.
- Re-scoped (decision 1(a)), it reports an honest bracket.
- It meets the L4BCTU gate's bracketing outcome without a third fix round.
- MATLAB parity requires no more.

Decisions 1–9 are in section 0.

### A.1 rvbBuild: IP4PC3/ELT76F/L4BCTU families, PCG(seed, 44044), from scratchpad w44review/rvB

The listing follows the probe file `zz_elt2_rvbbuild_test.go` (171 lines).
```go
type rvbCase struct {
	sys    *System
	oracle []complex128
	rank   int
}

func rvbBuild(t *testing.T, fam string, seed uint64) rvbCase {
	rng := rand.New(rand.NewPCG(seed, 44044))
	var fd, wd []float64
	cpx := false
	var ca, cb, cw float64
	stiffW := func() float64 { return math.Pow(10, -6.5-3.5*rng.Float64()) }
	reg := func() (float64, float64) { return rng.NormFloat64() * math.Pow(10, rng.Float64()*2-1), 0.5 + rng.Float64() }
	nreg := rng.IntN(3)
	switch fam {
	case "cpx":
		cpx = true
		cw = stiffW()
		ca, cb = rng.NormFloat64(), math.Abs(rng.NormFloat64())+0.1
		if rng.IntN(3) == 0 {
			ca = -math.Abs(ca)
		}
	case "two":
		for range 2 {
			fd = append(fd, rng.NormFloat64())
			wd = append(wd, stiffW())
		}
	case "smallLam":
		w := stiffW()
		fd, wd = append(fd, w*rng.NormFloat64()*math.Pow(10, 3*rng.Float64())), append(wd, w)
		nreg = 1 + rng.IntN(2)
	case "tri":
		fd, wd = append(fd, rng.NormFloat64()), append(wd, stiffW())
		nreg = 1 + rng.IntN(3)
	case "bigA":
		fd, wd = append(fd, rng.NormFloat64()), append(wd, stiffW())
		fd, wd = append(fd, math.Copysign(math.Pow(10, 2+4*rng.Float64()), rng.NormFloat64())), append(wd, 1)
	case "unstS":
		fd, wd = append(fd, math.Abs(rng.NormFloat64())), append(wd, stiffW())
		for range 1 + rng.IntN(2) {
			fd, wd = append(fd, -math.Abs(rng.NormFloat64())-0.05), append(wd, 0.5+rng.Float64())
		}
		nreg = 0
	case "edge":
		// stiff singular value near the stiff-band boundaries
		fd, wd = append(fd, rng.NormFloat64()), append(wd, math.Pow(10, -5.5-1.5*rng.Float64()-5*float64(rng.IntN(2))*rng.Float64()))
	default:
		t.Fatal(fam)
	}
	for range nreg {
		f, w := reg()
		fd, wd = append(fd, f), append(wd, w)
	}
	nf := len(fd)
	if cpx {
		nf += 2
	}
	chains := [][]int{{2}, {3}, {4}, {5}, {2, 2}, {2, 3}, {1, 2}, {3, 1}, {6}}[rng.IntN(9)]
	n := nf
	for _, k := range chains {
		n += k
	}
	F, W := mat.NewDense(n, n, nil), mat.NewDense(n, n, nil)
	var oracle []complex128
	o := 0
	if cpx {
		F.Set(0, 0, ca)
		F.Set(0, 1, cb)
		F.Set(1, 0, -cb)
		F.Set(1, 1, ca)
		W.Set(0, 0, cw)
		W.Set(1, 1, cw)
		oracle = append(oracle, complex(ca/cw, cb/cw), complex(ca/cw, -cb/cw))
		o = 2
	}
	tri := fam == "tri" || rng.IntN(2) == 0
	for i := range fd {
		F.Set(o+i, o+i, fd[i])
		W.Set(o+i, o+i, wd[i])
		oracle = append(oracle, complex(fd[i]/wd[i], 0))
		if tri {
			for j := o + i + 1; j < nf; j++ {
				F.Set(o+i, j, rng.NormFloat64())
				W.Set(o+i, j, 0.3*rng.NormFloat64())
			}
		}
	}
	o = nf
	for _, k := range chains {
		for i := range k {
			F.Set(o+i, o+i, 1)
			if i+1 < k {
				W.Set(o+i, o+i+1, 1)
			}
		}
		if rng.IntN(2) == 0 {
			for j := o; j < o+k; j++ {
				for i := range nf {
					F.Set(i, j, 0.5*rng.NormFloat64())
				}
			}
		}
		o += k
	}
	logCond := 2 * rng.Float64()
	mk := func() *mat.Dense {
		g := mat.NewDense(n, n, nil)
		for i := range n {
			for j := range n {
				g.Set(i, j, rng.NormFloat64())
			}
		}
		var qr mat.QR
		qr.Factorize(g)
		var q mat.Dense
		qr.QTo(&q)
		for j := range n {
			s := math.Pow(10, -logCond*float64(j)/float64(max(1, n-1)))
			for i := range n {
				q.Set(i, j, q.At(i, j)*s)
			}
		}
		g2 := mat.NewDense(n, n, nil)
		for i := range n {
			for j := range n {
				g2.Set(i, j, rng.NormFloat64())
			}
		}
		qr.Factorize(g2)
		var q2, out mat.Dense
		qr.QTo(&q2)
		out.Mul(&q, &q2)
		return &out
	}
	U, V := mk(), mk()
	var T, A, E, B, C mat.Dense
	T.Mul(U, F)
	A.Mul(&T, V)
	T.Mul(U, W)
	E.Mul(&T, V)
	b := mat.NewDense(n, 1, nil)
	c := mat.NewDense(1, n, nil)
	for i := range n {
		b.Set(i, 0, rng.NormFloat64())
		c.Set(0, i, rng.NormFloat64())
	}
	B.Mul(U, b)
	C.Mul(c, V)
	sys, err := NewDescriptor(&A, &B, &C, mat.NewDense(1, 1, []float64{0.1}), &E, 0)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	return rvbCase{sys, oracle, n - len(chains)}
}
```

### A.3 C1 jitter certificate (probe)

```go
type l4bEig struct {
	w    complex128
	move float64
	inf  bool
}

func l4bQZ(A, E *mat.Dense) ([]complex128, []bool, bool) {
	n, _ := A.Dims()
	ar, er := A.RawMatrix(), E.RawMatrix()
	alphar, alphai, beta, ok := qzEigenvalues(n, ar.Data, ar.Stride, er.Data, er.Stride)
	if !ok {
		return nil, nil, false
	}
	infTol := qzInfiniteTol(100*float64(n)*eps(), mat.Norm(A, 2), mat.Norm(E, 2))
	w := make([]complex128, n)
	inf := make([]bool, n)
	for i := range n {
		inf[i] = qzInfinite(alphar[i], alphai[i], beta[i], infTol)
		if !inf[i] {
			w[i] = complex(alphar[i]/beta[i], alphai[i]/beta[i])
		}
	}
	return w, inf, true
}

func l4bJitterCert(A, E *mat.Dense) ([]l4bEig, bool) {
	w, inf, ok := l4bQZ(A, E)
	if !ok {
		return nil, false
	}
	out := make([]l4bEig, len(w))
	for i := range w {
		out[i] = l4bEig{w: w[i], inf: inf[i]}
	}
	rng := rand.New(rand.NewPCG(3, 5))
	jitter := func(m *mat.Dense) *mat.Dense {
		c := mat.DenseCopyOf(m)
		raw := c.RawMatrix()
		for i := range raw.Rows {
			row := raw.Data[i*raw.Stride : i*raw.Stride+raw.Cols]
			for j := range row {
				row[j] *= 1 + 4*eps()*(2*rng.Float64()-1)
			}
		}
		return c
	}
	for range leakDraws {
		g, ginf, gok := l4bQZ(jitter(A), jitter(E))
		if !gok {
			return nil, false
		}
		for i := range out {
			if out[i].inf {
				continue
			}
			best := math.Inf(1)
			for j := range g {
				if !ginf[j] {
					best = min(best, cmplx.Abs(g[j]-out[i].w)/cmplx.Abs(out[i].w))
				}
			}
			out[i].move = max(out[i].move, best)
		}
	}
	return out, true
}

func l4bCertCount(es []l4bEig) int {
	c := 0
	for _, e := range es {
		if !e.inf && e.move <= leakStableTol {
			c++
		}
	}
	return c
}
```

### A.4 O4 classifier at 2^-k

It uses `pencilDetPoly`, `polyRoots`, `bcAbs2`, `bcSub` and `polyRootPrec` from `descriptor_pole_count_oracle_test.go` on origin/parked/descriptor-elt76f-staircase 76a7a1e. The probe calls `l4bClassify(n, a, e, 53, seed)` for seeds 100, 101 and 102.

```go
func l4bClassify(n int, a, e []float64, k uint, seed uint64) poleCountSensitivity {
	rat := func(x []float64, pert *rand.Rand) []*big.Rat {
		out := make([]*big.Rat, len(x))
		for i, v := range x {
			out[i] = new(big.Rat).SetFloat64(v)
			if pert != nil {
				f := new(big.Rat).SetInt64(1)
				d := new(big.Rat).SetFrac(big.NewInt(1), new(big.Int).Lsh(big.NewInt(1), k))
				if pert.IntN(2) == 0 {
					f.Add(f, d)
				} else {
					f.Sub(f, d)
				}
				out[i].Mul(out[i], f)
			}
		}
		return out
	}
	rng := rand.New(rand.NewPCG(seed, 53))
	z0, ok0 := polyRoots(pencilDetPoly(n, rat(a, nil), rat(e, nil)))
	z1, ok1 := polyRoots(pencilDetPoly(n, rat(a, rng), rat(e, rng)))
	out := poleCountSensitivity{OK: ok0 && ok1}
	used := make([]bool, len(z1))
	for _, r := range z0 {
		best, bd := -1, (*big.Float)(nil)
		for j, q := range z1 {
			if used[j] {
				continue
			}
			if d := bcAbs2(bcSub(r, q)); best < 0 || d.Cmp(bd) < 0 {
				best, bd = j, d
			}
		}
		used[best] = true
		rel := new(big.Float).SetPrec(polyRootPrec).Quo(bd, bcAbs2(r))
		f, _ := rel.Float64()
		out.Roots = append(out.Roots, r.complex128())
		out.S = append(out.S, math.Sqrt(f))
	}
	return out
}
```

## Coordinator rulings on the design proposal (wave 56, advisor-reviewed); recorded before any code
**C2 is APPROVED as the framing, and is complete ONLY with decision 9 = yes.** A documented resolution limit on an unlabelled value is rejected (CEFUJP/DBOVA4/UEG4D5). L4BCTU stays NON-DONE as the live definition of "finite".

1. **The perturbation model is (a), normwise (LAPACK/MATLAB-rank class).**
   - F1 parity is decided by the LAPACK class; MATLAB's own output is unverified.
   - Observation (b), cpx:2531 robust under 2^-53 yet dropped by QZ, is the route for a future extended-precision path. That is a PERF-gated follow-up task, out of scope now.
2. **"Never fewer than Hi":** retire it as an asserted invariant if Hi is the whole-pencil QZ count; keep it as a census column.
   - Clarification sent to the coordinator: Hi here is the parked 320-bit exact staircase's upper bracket (76a7a1e certifyFinitePoleCount), not the QZ count. Pending re-rule.
3. **Exclusion guard: FAIL, not pass-with-reason.** Before C2 covers rvb two and cpx, produce a per-row table showing each excluded row is (i) in the F1 band under (a) AND (ii) that the bracket contains the oracle count.
   - All rows in: the guard is re-ruled per family as a recorded DECISION carrying the table.
   - Any row out: it is a miss and the guard stands.
4. **C1 is census-only** (38 value->error, 32 new arch flips).
5. **Do not close 4ZWFL5.**
   - cpx:17 (amd64 nf=8 ok vs arm64 nf=0 !ok, over-count by 5 on structural 3) is NOT a resolution limit, which would be ±1 at a band edge. It is filed as its own CORE task, and 4ZWFL5 depends on it.
   - No pinned flip rate (110/1500 would be a tuned constant). The pin is "bracket contains oracle", per row.
6. **C3: no as code.** Make it a census column first. Promote it only if every fire is a base-wrong row.
7. **IP4PC3 fast path:** conditional on (a). It is an IP4PC3 round, not a design item. Census the yield first; if it is 0, don't write it.
8. **5CNIZA:** trim the body only after verifying that 410/40/250 still fail on current main. Pin 159/45 as topic-named regression tests if nothing covers them.
9. **YES. This is C2's one production change.** It follows the C2D/C2DFit pattern:
   - Poles is unchanged (parity).
   - A diagnostic sibling returns the poles, the Lo/Hi bracket and Accuracy (riccati 0/1 semantics).
   - Match the library's existing diagnostic-sibling naming. The name and shape are proposed to the coordinator BEFORE code.
   - ELT76F and 4ZWFL5 (minus cpx:17) then close against the label, not a count.
   - 2WPHMT's Accuracy surface is the same question: keep it consistent and rule both together.

**Unverified items** (F3 Lo patch, C3 yield, MATLAB, w26Gen 107, 5CNIZA 410/40/250) each get a probe before any ruling relies on them. E664VD as a separate class is acknowledged.

title: DECISION (decided, live): TunePIDFRD certification done-bar for sampled FRD data (supersedes pruned XTCC7X)
body:
Re-filed 2026-10-26 from XTCC7X (pruned; quoted verbatim from git f86231f:.ergo/backlog.jsonl). DECISION record: kept as draft so it is never pruned or picked up as ready work. Amendments below are part of the operative bar.

## Original (XTCC7X, 2026-10-25)
DECIDED 2026-10-25 (advisor, per advisor-for-decisions; coordinator request). Scope: TunePIDFRD certification on sampled FRD data. Not TunePID (HEOZ5K, YRNRQP, ZHTUBP, PC4MF4, S7ERV4 out of scope).

MATLAB basis: pidtune doc defines info.Stable only as "1 if the closed loop is stable, and 0 otherwise"; for frd plants it relies on the user-supplied unstable-pole count (pidtuneOptions) and does not say how Stable is verified from samples. So the certified flag is stricter than MATLAB and the bar is ours; only 3N3NG2 (never fail, return uncertified with warning) is parity. https://www.mathworks.com/help/control/ref/dynamicsystem.pidtune.html

1. Certified = Nyquist count known from data AND every crossing used for reported margins read from a resolved step. Does not mean the PM target was met (AchievedPhaseMargin < target is allowed and visible).
2. Resolved step: trusted fit (pidTuningFRDTrusted(StepFits)), or smooth-step cubic gate passes (pidTuningFRDSmoothCrossing), or chord with no |L|-1 sign change and |L|-1 not within eps of 0 at either end. Band ends anchored per pidTuningFRDTopFlat / pidTuningFRDLowCrossings.
3. Guarantees on a CERTIFIED design (violation = bug, checked vs dense oracle): oracle-stable; reported PM <= dense PM + 1.5 deg; reported |S| >= dense peak / 1.05 (and certified implies dense |S| <= 4 within that slack); HARD RULE: design and error identical to base for every oracle-robust case. Certification granted on an unresolved step is a bug.
4. Documented limits (close, don't fix): any margin discrepancy on an UNCERTIFIED design; loss of certification when a pole/zero sits within ~10x above hi or below lo; loss of certification on noisy data; reporting error inside tolerance (incl. under-reports).
5. Search stays chord-based. A search change is an optional separate CORE task whose acceptance is zero design changes among oracle-robust cases in the 2800-case sweep.
6. Done-bar test: one persistent sweep test over fixed seeds of the standard families asserting item 3 for every certified design; skipSlowUnderRace.
Filing cutoff: no new TunePIDFRD task unless it violates item 3 on a certified design or certifies an unresolved step. Everything else goes into the sweep summary as a limit.
Folds 7WK6K5 (its search items = item 5).

## Amendment 1 (2026-10-26, PR #370, accepted by coordinator/advisor): item 2 widened for chord crossings
A chord crossing strictly inside an unmarked step counts as RESOLVED if any of: a step fit read a crossing in that step (lone fits included); trusted StepFits exist; the smooth-step cubic gate passes; or no polynomial reading (chord at w, cubic, both quadratics through neighbouring samples; non-crossing interpolants ignored) is more than 1.5 deg below the achieved margin. Otherwise the design is uncertified ("not certified ... nor its margins"). Reason: the literal item-2 reading uncertified ~10% of accurate certified designs (19/136 res, 7/49 sparse, 1/93 strict); the widened rule loses only violators plus item-4 limit cases.

## Amendment 2 (2026-10-26, QHMGQL ruling, coordinator/advisor)
Item 4 "limits" cover only what the certifier REPORTS as unknown (uncertified). They never excuse a design the certifier certified: any certified design violating item 3 is a CORE bug, wherever the hidden dynamics sit (e.g. resonance beyond the ~10x TopFlat zone). For ideal-derivative (Tf=0) designs: do not anchor/certify the Markov end unless |L(inf)| is well below 1; gains unchanged, uncertified with warning (3N3NG2), never fail, never estimate true PM from data lacking the resonance. Guardrail: 2600-case base-vs-branch sweep; if accurate ideal-PID designs lose certification beyond a handful, narrow the gate (e.g. tie the |L(inf)| threshold to TopFlat curvature) rather than loosen the bar.

## Note
Decision tasks are not pruned: keep them as drafts (never done), so `ergo prune` cannot remove them.

## Amendment 3 (2026-10-26, QHMGQL ruling, coordinator/advisor): ideal-derivative Markov end is never certified
For continuous ideal-derivative designs (Tf = 0, Kd != 0) the Markov end 1 + Kd*m is never certified from sampled data; the design is returned unchanged with a "not certified" warning that names the cause (no roll-off) and suggests PIDF (Tf > 0) (3N3NG2). Documented limit of band-limited data: L does not roll off, so a pole pair of damping zeta anywhere above the band lifts |L| by about 1/(2 zeta), and band-limited samples bound neither zeta nor the distance. Rejected alternative: a zeta_min floor (threshold 2*zeta_min) is a heuristic constant no reference library uses (matlab-parity rule) and would knowingly admit certified violators (amendment 2).
Evidence (wave 30, fix/pid-wave30): 3300 seeded base-vs-branch cases (strict, resonance, sparse, top-cut, resonance-sparse x520, plus hidden-pair family PCG 7702): 0 design or error changes; certified done-bar violators 24 on base -> 0 of 3300 on branch. Cost: 43 accurate ideal-D designs in the 2600 standard cases lose certification (~9.4% of base-certified), still returned with the warning. The narrower gate (|L(inf)|<=0.5 or TopFlat bend<=TopCurvature/3) leaked 42/1200 hidden-pair violators.

title: DECISION (decided, live): descriptor E rank = MATLAB rank (n*eps(sigma_1)) via descriptorRank; luNearSingular never declares E deficient
body:
DECIDED 2026-10-26 (advisor, per advisor-for-decisions). DECISION record: kept as draft so it is never pruned.

Rule: the numerical rank of a descriptor E is MATLAB rank(E): default tolerance max(size(E))*eps(norm(E)) = n*eps(sigma_1) on the singular values (https://www.mathworks.com/help/matlab/ref/rank.html). In controlsys this is exactly descriptorRank(sv, sv[0], n, full=true) (floor n*ulp(sigma_1)), already the D62TAA SLICOT/MATLAB rule. It is the only arbiter of "E singular / rank deficient" for ToExplicit, TransferFunction, IsProper, Step and the descriptor reduction.

luNearSingular (matutil.go: cond estimate * eps >= 1, or NaN/Inf) is a heuristic and must NOT declare E rank deficient ahead of the SVD rule. It may stay only as a conservative cheap exit in the other direction (lu.Cond()*10n^2*eps < 1 => full rank, as in eRankDeficient) or for an exact zero pivot. Call sites that use luNearSingular as a rank decision on E fall under this ruling: state_space_utils.go eRankDeficient (line ~99), descriptor.go ~97/116/652/1044 (check each: E rank vs solve-conditioning use). Non-descriptor uses (canon, controller, inv, convert, transform, matrix_equation_problem, conversion_delay) are solve-conditioning checks, out of scope.
FreqResponse solves (sE-A) directly and does not use E rank; confirm when implementing.

Consequence: models with sigma_n ~ eps*sigma_1 (k ~ 0.8-1.2 in rv30rNSE) read full rank, as MATLAB does. VDATJL (seed 1624 TF error) is this symptom and is folded into the implementation task. More near-boundary models then flow through the stiff explicit path, so WOIVWF (Step off for ill-conditioned E) may grow in count: that is MATLAB ss(dss) parity, not a regression.
Implementation: CORE task filed separately; queue after #374 (touches state_space_utils.go, transfer.go).

Scope note (wave 33): Low priority: requireNonsingular in descriptor.go:116 (lqr/icare-type entry points through newControllerObserverPolicy) still rejects E on luNearSingular (cond*eps >= 1) when MATLAB rank(E) is full. The coordinator can extend RL6IT7 there if MATLAB lqr(dss) parity calls for it. The likely trigger is the existing test model fullRankNearSingularE(t, 2.46e-15) in descriptor_e_rank_test.go passed to an lqr/kalman entry point. Not run, so whether MATLAB itself rejects this E is not established. Pending owner/advisor decision whether lqr/kalman/lqg descriptor entry points (requireNonsingular, descriptor.go:116) follow this rule; needs Riccati accuracy evidence before moving models from error to value.

## Amendment 1 (2026-10-26, advisor; coordinator asked): lqr/kalman/lqg descriptor entry points
MATLAB basis: lqr Tips: "lqr supports descriptor models with nonsingular E"; S is the Riccati solution "for the equivalent explicit state-space model" (https://www.mathworks.com/help/control/ref/lti.lqr.html). MATLAB states no rank test, so "nonsingular" follows this decision: MATLAB rank(E) full = nonsingular.
Ruling: descriptorPolicy.requireNonsingular (descriptor.go, used by newControllerObserverPolicy for Lqr/Kalman/Lqg/Lqi family) uses the RL6IT7 rule (descriptorRank full=true), not luNearSingular. Admission is not a value: newly admitted models go through the E-aware Riccati path (model E passed to Care/Dare), and the design is returned only if verifyRiccati certifies it honestly (ZLHTCH/D3WPCL honesty rule); otherwise ErrDescriptorSingular/ErrNoStabilizing as before. No explicit E^-1 fold for these.
Implementation: CORE task (filed separately); guardrail: rv30rNSE-class sweep k in [0.5,2] through Lqr/Kalman/Lqg vs 320-bit oracle, assert Accuracy honesty, zero correct->wrong, report error->value counts. Queue after #376 (descriptor.go) and D3WPCL (riccati.go) merge.

## Amendment 2 (2026-10-26, advisor; supersedes amendment 1 admission rule): Riccati entry points
Evidence (wave 35, M23EGI): rejecting on MATLAB rank alone strands 50+ base Lqr values that the 320-bit oracle shows correct AND robust to eps perturbations of E (window B: MATLAB rank deficient by a hair, LU cond*eps<1). No value->error outranks amendment 1.
Rule: for IsProper/TF/Step/ToExplicit, MATLAB rank alone decides (E rank IS the answer). For Riccati entry points (descriptorPolicy.requireNonsingular, riccatiDescriptor), "nonsingular E" is a solver precondition that MATLAB lqr states without a tolerance: admit when MATLAB rank is full OR LU cond*eps<1 (reject only when both say singular). Union of two existing rules, no new constant. Honesty comes from the gates, not admission: verifyRiccati + nearSingularEGate cancellation screen + Kalman dual via plantE. Known exception: Kalmd keeps the old LU rejection (folds E^-1 unverified).
Lqi: judge the PLANT E, not blkdiag(E,I): rank(blkdiag(E,I)) = rank(E)+p exactly; the augmented tolerance (n+p)*eps*max(sigma1,1) is a scaling artifact when sigma1(E)<1. Implementation is a follow-up task in controller.go.

## Amendment 3 (2026-10-26, advisor; from YW5B4U amendment 1, PR #380): Stabsep/Modsep stiff full-rank mode
Evidence (PR #380): a descriptor G1 = (S11, T11) carrying the stiff mode has t_ii ~3e-16 and fails MATLAB rank by the same RL6IT7 rule that made the mode finite, so Poles(G1) would drop it again (the EJYYFD class one level down). Review: 2400 broad + 1983 targeted cases, native and amd64, zero regressions; G1+G2 matches the pencil to 1e-9 at five frequencies.
Principle: the invariant governs over the mechanism. A representation that fails the rule that made the mode finite cannot carry that mode.
Rule:
1. A stiff beta=0 mode of a full-rank E is added to the part isGroup1(lambda) selects as an explicit decoupled state (lambda, b/beta, c). G1 stays explicit; no type change for any model base handled correctly. MATLAB "same type as G" holds in the class sense (dss is ss).
2. G2 becomes explicit only under the decomposeGeneralized trigger, quoted verbatim:
   if sawInfinite && nf == a.RawMatrix().Rows {
       if lambda, ok := stiffFullRankPole(sys.A, sys.E); ok && (n1 > 0 || isGroup1(lambda)) {
   i.e. the selector rejected a beta~0 mode AND deflateInfinite deflated nothing (full-rank E). On a full-rank E that trigger is exactly "base dropped a finite pole", so no model base handled correctly enters this path.
Residual: tiny nonzero beta outside the class is tracked under HK6D3N.

## Amendment 4 (2026-10-27, advisor; HK6D3N, PR wave 37): Stabsep/Modsep tiny nonzero beta
Same principle as amendment 3, applied to the tiny-nonzero-beta case the beta=0 wording did not cover. Gate quoted verbatim from decomposeGeneralized:
    if n := nf; !sawInfinite && n == a.RawMatrix().Rows && n1 < n &&
        descriptorERankDeficient(extractModalBlock(t, n, n1, n, n1, n)) && !descriptorERankDeficient(sys.E) {
        if lambda, tol, ok := stiffTinyBetaPole(sys.A, sys.E); ok {
            if g1, g2, ok := splitStiffFullRank(...); ok && (g2.E == nil || !descriptorERankDeficient(g2.E)) {
i.e. G2's T22 fails MATLAB rank while sys.E does not; accepted only if the resulting G2 is not rank deficient; otherwise base. It can only restore a dropped pole. Evidence: 1.81M op lines native + 308k amd64, 37+8 changed lines, all restoring a dropped pole, 0 IsStable flips on sys or parts, 0 errors.
stiffRatioGap (new constant, 10x) survives the no-invented-constants rule only because it decides WHETHER TO ATTEMPT the repair (which eigenvalue is the isolated stiff one), never WHAT THE ANSWER IS: the result is checked by the rank invariant and falls back to base.

## Amendment 5 (2026-10-27, advisor; HK6D3N): scope of "agree with the explicit model"
The EJYYFD/amendment-3 agreement tiebreak was for the beta=0 deflation artifact (QZ the broken party, finiteness from MATLAB rank). It means "do not drop a finite mode", not "Poles inherits the fold's values". Poles/IsStable are the pencil (MATLAB pole(dss) = eig(A,E)). The agreement rule covers E rank and finite-mode retention, not pole values.
ToExplicit (E^-1 A fold): when ||E^-1 A|| ~ 1/eps any float64 rounding moves slow eigenvalues O(1); a representation limit of the explicit form. MATLAB ss(sys,'explicit') documents no alternative method (https://www.mathworks.com/help/control/ref/ss.html), so ToExplicit's output stays the explicit model by contract and is a documented limit. HK6D3N evidence: 822 (oracle agrees with Poles/QZ, stable) : 0 (agrees with fold) : 7 (flips under eps perturbation); 0 stiff-sign disagreements in 55k+ models. Step/C2D, which simulate the fold, are handled under WOIVWF (CORE).

Amendment 6 (advisor + coordinator ruling, wave 38 WOIVWF): descriptor-native routing of full-rank ill-conditioned E. Impulse (time domain) routes at the stiffPencilSplit gate (LU cond(E) >= 1e4 before and after equilibration, full MATLAB rank): the fold impulse is wrong from 1e4 (2799 of 2809 well-posed sweep rows), so case (b), correctness wins. C2D (all methods except matched), Step and zero-x0 Lsim route only when the raw LU cond(E) >= foldAccurateECond = 1e6 (convert.go foldInaccurateParts), because the LU fold is within tolerance in [1e4, 1e6): C2D 324 fold-ok vs 1 fold-wrong, Step 295 vs 2 (9300-model sweep, 320-bit pencil oracle), so case (a). This brings mild-cond C2D from 2.4x to 1.34x vs base. Raw (not equilibrated) cond is the feature, because ToExplicit factorizes the raw E. Matched C2D uses the pencil transfer function whenever stiffDescriptorParts applies.
Amendment 7: Step/C2D use splitFastPencil (3+ parts); TransferFunction stays two-part stiffExplicitParts until task UOFXRA unifies them.
Amendment 8: stiffModalHold changes explicit-model C2D ZOH/FOH/impulse and Step (rho(A)*dt >= 1e3, quasi-triangular or all-stiff A; dense mixed-mode unchanged). Accepted on a 6000-model explicit sweep (0 correct->wrong) and a fohKernel-caller probe (C2D FOH, C2DMap FOH, fractional-delay FOH channel/LFT, D2C FOH: 0 correct->wrong, 0 value->error vs base). Fractional-delay FOH stays wrong on both trees (task RR43HG).

Amendment 9 (advisor, wave 45 AZUMSC): Initial and Lsim with nonzero x0 route at the same gate as Step and zero-x0 Lsim: raw LU cond(E) >= foldAccurateECond (1e6, via foldInaccurateParts/foldInaccurateContinuous), no I/O delay, no LFT. This supersedes am.6's "zero-x0" qualifier. Reasons: Lsim must not switch routes between x0=0 and x0=eps; the fold's Initial was < 1e-7 on 283/283 well-posed models in [1e4, 1e6); round 2 found 0 correct->wrong in 3100 cases. Mechanism: a separate pencil split of the free response (stiffFreeParts/addStiffFreeSamples), not an A*x0 step augmentation. That augmentation cancels C*x0 against C*z in the tail, and its error grew with |x0| (gen 1331: 1.2e-5, now 1.0e-8). Delayed C2D: non-matched methods build a parallel explicit model (stiffDescriptorExplicit, realSchurPart per am.8) at the same 1e6 gate. Matched with delays keeps the descriptor at the existing delay-free matched route (stiffDescriptorParts) and returns the delay-free result times z^-k.

### am.10 (wave 47, XWFTRV; advisor ruling) — supersedes am.9's "no I/O delay" qualifier
am.6/am.9 routing (Impulse at stiffPencilSplit; Step/Lsim/Initial at raw LU cond(E) >= 1e6) applies with I/O delays (no LFT), via ioDelayFreeCore. Impulse samples shifted parts exactly (shiftedStiffImpulse); free response shifts per OutputDelay; Delay matrix without I/O split still ErrDelayUnsupported. Step/Lsim with off-grid delays carry RR43HG residue (test stepTol 1e-5; tighten to 1e-7 after RR43HG). Side effect: base's auto horizon collapsed to the delay on delayed stiff models; fixed.

The 027664e-vs-HEAD benchcmp shows my commits leave time unchanged, so this all comes from 027664e. Cause: every automatic first design now builds newPidtuneGate, which samples about 9+ decades ([floor*1e-3, wc*1e3]) even when the design then passes. Files: pidtune.go (Pidtune, run.design(wc, sign, auto), newPidtuneGate). Narrowing the band or building the gate lazily could change gate verdicts, so this is an owner decision; not fixed.

Pidtune small automatic calls still cost about 470us vs 77us on 8cfed86 (Pidtune_PI/PID/PIDF, FastSampled ~2.6x). Cause: AUOTFB gates every auto first design on the full back-off gate grid, [floor*1e-3, wc*1e3] at 1% steps (about 2100 plant solves, pidtune.go newPidtuneGate). Lowering it means building the first design's grid lazily or narrowing it, which changes verdicts on some plants; that needs an owner decision.

Perf: BenchmarkPidtune_Delayed/PD (0.3s-1/(s+1)^4, input delay 5, PD, wc=0) is 1.1-1.2ms on base and about 18-28ms now. The gated first design (|S| 7.6) fails, all 60 back-off steps run gate checks and fail, then the ungated first design is returned as the fallback. A faster failing gate path or an earlier stop (e.g. when |S| rises steadily as wc drops) would recover this. File: pidtune.go (Pidtune back-off loop).

Perf (minor, existing pattern): on the reflected-delay path, r.screened(wc) and checkPidtuneStability each call screen.at(wc, family), which builds pidTuningDelayStability state twice per step that reaches Nyquist. The same double call happens on the non-delay gated path (r.gated(pid, wc, r.screened(wc))). Files: pidtune.go (pidtuneRun.check), pid_tuning.go (pidStabilityScreen.at).

BenchmarkPidtune_BackoffFail/GateP is +7% (3.52 to 3.77 ms) after the crossover scan moved to the finer |S| grid (16add00). Repro: benchcmp -base b0e01b5 -candidate 9b2e8d4 -bench ^BenchmarkPidtune. Most of it is bisection and golden-section refinement calls into the memoized p.at during back-off steps that fail anyway.
